brief: Approving a 13-storey building at 1464 King Street West with 80 homes including 19 replacement rentals, plus shops, a daycare and a temple goes to City Council for a decision.

title: 1497 and 1501 Queen Street West and 89 and 91 Beaty Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws
brief: City Council is set to decide whether to approve two mixed-use buildings (10 and 7 storeys) at Queen Street West and Beaty Avenue, with 141 affordable rental homes including 54 replacements, keeping the historic storefronts. The city waived $105,028 in planning fees for the affordable homes.

title: 2273, 2277 and 2279 Bloor Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment - Approval
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve a 15-storey building at 2273 to 2279 Bloor Street West with 60 homes and shops.

title: 355 Adelaide Street West - Construction Staging Area
brief: It's City Council's call whether to approve closing the eastbound curb lane on Adelaide Street West near Charlotte Street from January 2027 to December 2028, for construction of a 58-storey condo at 355 Adelaide Street West.

title: Richmond Street West (471 Richmond Street West and 38 Camden Street) - Construction Staging Area
topics: parking prohibitions, parking regulations, traffic regulations
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve closing the sidewalk and the westbound lane on the south side of Richmond Street West from August 2026 to April 2029, with a temporary walkway, for construction staging at 471 Richmond Street West.

title: 1 Bloor Street West (Yonge Street at Bloor Street West) - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
brief: The decision on whether to extend the construction closure on Yonge Street south of Bloor from January 2027 to June 2028, to finish the 85-storey tower at 1 Bloor Street West rests with City Council.

title: Noble Street (1266 Queen Street West) - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, parking prohibitions, parking regulations, traffic regulations
brief: Before City Council for a decision: approve construction staging on Noble Street from December 2026 to November 2028 — sidewalk and lane closures plus a temporary one-way — for a 27-storey condo at 1266 Queen Street West.

title: Donlands Avenue - Parking Amendments
brief: Whether to make a corner parking ban on Donlands Avenue stricter, keeping the curb clear for better sightlines and safer school pickup and drop-off now sits with City Council.

title: College Street and Manning Avenue - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
brief: City Council will decide whether to install traffic lights at College Street and Manning Avenue to make the crossing safer for walkers, and to ban mid-block crossings on College Street at Manning.

title: Avenue Road and Edmund Avenue/Private Access - Traffic Control Signal Amendments
brief: City Council decides whether to update the traffic lights at Avenue Road and Edmund Avenue to include a private driveway from De La Salle College, with new turn bans to keep it one-way and limit spillover traffic.

title: 1134 Queen Street East - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
brief: Whether to extend the construction closure on Queen Street East near Bertmount Avenue from October 2026 to March 2027, to finish a three-storey condo with shops at 1134 Queen Street East now sits with City Council.

title: Temporary Adjustments to Traffic and Parking Regulations for 2026 Distillery Winter Village (Non-Delegated)
brief: A decision on approving the matching set of temporary traffic and parking rules for the 2026 Distillery Winter Village on transit-served streets that only city council can change sits with City Council.

title: 47-65 Huntley Street, 2-18, 24, and 26 Linden Street and 1-11 Selby Street - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will decide whether to allow the demolition of 29 rental homes at Huntley, Selby and Linden streets, replaced by 29 rental units, with $20,000.00 in tenant compensation.

title: 325 Gerrard Street East - Construction Staging Area
brief: Whether to approve closing the east sidewalk and part of the southbound lane on Dreamers Way from July 2026 to September 2029, for a 26-storey mixed-use building at 325 Gerrard Street East now sits with City Council.

title: 350 Davenport Road - Construction Staging Area
brief: A decision on closing the east sidewalk, bike lane and lanes on Davenport Road near Dupont from August 2026 to August 2028, with walkway and bike detours, for an eight-storey project at 350 Davenport Road goes to City Council. Eight $4.50-per-hour parking spaces would be temporarily removed.

title: Dufferin Street and Florence Street - Traffic Control Signals
topics: traffic control systems, traffic regulations, transportation
brief: The call on whether to install traffic lights at Dufferin Street and Florence Street, replacing an existing crosswalk, to improve safety for walkers and cyclists belongs to City Council.

title: Metrolinx Ontario Line - Long-Term Temporary Road Closures, Temporary Delegation of Authority and Update on Liberty New Street
topics: parking regulations, road closures, traffic regulations, transportation
brief: The decision on whether to approve long-term lane and sidewalk closures from 2026 to 2030 for building the Ontario Line's Gerrard and Leslieville stations, plus letting staff adjust traffic measures as work proceeds rests with City Council. The report references parking machine rates of $3 and $3.25 per hour.

title: Eglinton Avenue East and Lillian Street - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
topics: pedestrianization, public safety, traffic signal control systems
brief: City Council will decide whether to install traffic lights at Eglinton Avenue East and Lillian Street, where the TTC runs a service, to make the crossing safer for walkers and other vulnerable road users.

title: Elizabeth Street and Elm Street - Traffic Control Signals
topics: pedestrians, safety, traffic control systems, traffic regulations
pedestrianization, public safety, traffic signal control systems
brief: City Council is set to decide whether to install traffic lights at Elm Street and Elizabeth Street, replacing the current all-way stop, to improve safety for everyone.

title: Temporary Adjustments to Traffic and Parking Regulations for 2026 Canadian National Exhibition (Non-Delegated)
brief: The decision on approving the matching set of temporary traffic and parking rules for the 2026 CNE on transit-served streets that only city council can change rests with City Council.

title: Oriole Parkway - Parking By-law Amendments
brief: Changing parking rules on Oriole Parkway for a road resurfacing project that adds a tree-lined centre median, removing three paid parking spots is on City Council's agenda.

title: 181 to 195 Dundas Street West and 63 Centre Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve a 41-storey mixed-use building at Dundas Street West and Centre Avenue with retail, offices and 135 homes.

title: Chinatown Tomorrow Planning Initiative - Final Report
topics: Official Plans, activities in planning and development, development, planning
brief: City Council will decide whether to adopt the West Chinatown Planning Framework and related rule changes to guide future building, small business support, housing, public space and heritage protection in the area.
stake: About Official Plans. Decided by a recorded vote, 23 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Toronto Builds: 53 Strachan Avenue and 805 and 805A Wellington Street West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve an eight-storey building with 81 supportive homes and a 28-storey building with 296 homes, 60 affordable, at 53 Strachan Avenue and 805 Wellington Street West.

title: Toronto Builds: 78 Springhurst Avenue and 1 to 3 Close Avenue (Dunn House Phase 2) - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, social housing
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve an eight-storey rental building with 54 homes at 78 Springhurst Avenue, part of the Social Medicine Housing Initiative with University Health Network and United Way.

title: 324 Cherry Street and 429 and 455 Lake Shore Boulevard East - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve 14 buildings with ten towers of 28 to 53 storeys at Cherry Street and Lake Shore Boulevard East, with 4,969 homes, affordable housing and a childcare centre, with figures of $552, and $1103, in the report.

title: Initial Findings Report: Transit Priority Measures to Support the 505 Dundas 6-Minute Network
brief: This is a routine item: the community council is asked to receive a report with early results of transit priority measures on Dundas Street supporting more frequent 505 Dundas streetcars. No policy change is involved.
stake: About congestion. Decided by a recorded vote, 20 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: 955 Lake Shore Boulevard West - Temporary Left Turn Prohibitions
brief: Whether to ban left turns at a temporary construction entrance on Lake Shore Boulevard West, from August 2026 to August 2029, to keep traffic safe while the new Ontario Science Centre is built now sits with City Council.

title: Transit Priority Measures to Support Transit Diversions During Construction on King Street West
topics: stopping prohibitions, traffic regulations, turn prohibitions (traffic)
brief: Before City Council for a decision: approve temporary parking and traffic changes on King Street West from November 2026 to about May 2027, while streetcars are paused for watermain and track work.

title: 1650 Military Trail (Phase 2) - Construction Staging Area
brief: A construction staging area for an 8-storey student rental at 1650 Military Trail goes to City Council for approval. The project needs road and lane closures in two phases.

title: Fort York Integrated Operations and Heritage Stewardship Study
topics: community development, economic development, heritage designation
brief: This is a routine item. The community council will receive, for information, a report on plans for a study to coordinate how Fort York National Historic Site is managed, balancing heritage, programming and community use. No approval is being requested.

title: Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2565, 1 and 2 Meadowglen Place, R.A.B. PROPERTIES Limited/Lawrence Blankenstein
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council can take over the roads and sewers built for the subdivision at 1 and 2 Meadowglen Place. The developer finished the work under a 2019 agreement.

title: Guildwood Parkway - Traffic Regulations
brief: U-turns and some turns would be banned in front of Sir Wilfrid Laurier Collegiate Institute on Guildwood Parkway during school peak times. City Council is asked to approve.

title: 6600 Lawrence Avenue East - Permanent Closure of Portions of the Public Highway
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council can permanently close part of the public road at 6600 Lawrence Avenue East.

title: Danforth Avenue - Traffic Safety Improvements
topics: pedestrian islands, traffic control systems, traffic management
traffic operations, traffic signal control systems
brief: Road safety changes on Danforth Avenue at three spots, following a study of speeding and safety in Oakridge, go to City Council for approval.

title: Sheppard Avenue East at Massie Street and at a Point 390 Metres East of McCowan Road - Traffic Control Signals
topics: pedestrian islands, removal, traffic control systems
pedestrian refuge islands, traffic signal control systems
brief: Replacing two pedestrian islands on Sheppard Avenue East with traffic signals, at Massie Street and east of McCowan Road. It goes to City Council for approval.

title: Morrish Road Operational Closure at Highway 2A/Military Trail - Road Alteration
brief: City Council can close the south end of Morrish Road with a cul-de-sac and shut the Highway 2A off-ramp to Morrish Road. The changes are an interim step in the Highland Creek Village transport plan.

title: Lawrence Avenue East - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
brief: Two new pedestrian crossovers on Lawrence Avenue East, at Portwine Drive and west of Starspray Boulevard, go to City Council for approval.

title: Midland Avenue and Kilcullen Castle Gate - Traffic Control Signals
brief: Traffic signals at Midland Avenue and Kilcullen Castle Gate, which staff say are justified for safety, go to City Council for approval.

title: 1377 Sheppard Avenue West (Downsview West District) - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: land use, planning, urban planning, zoning, zoning bylaws, zoning designations
brief: Approving a large development at 1377 Sheppard Avenue West (Downsview West): 845,000 square metres of floor space, 6- to 60-storey buildings, and about 9,250 homes, with 10 percent of residential space secured. It goes to City Council for approval. The owner would also provide public art worth at least $1 million.

title: Warden Avenue and Continental Place/Private Access - Traffic Control Signals and Traffic Regulations
brief: Traffic signals on Warden Avenue at Continental Place, which staff say would make the crossing safer, go to City Council for approval.

title: 2025 Audited Financial Statements - Consolidated City, Sinking Funds, and Trust Funds
topics: annual reports, audits, capital budgets, financial reports
brief: Approving the City's 2025 financial statements. It goes to City Council for approval. The outside auditors gave clean opinions on all three sets of statements.

title: Audit of Solid Waste Management Services - Contract Management for Solid Waste Collections, Organics Processing Services and Construction Projects
topics: audits, construction, municipal services, organics (waste), solid waste management
auditors, building, city services, green bin materials
organic waste, solid waste management planning
brief: The Auditor General asks Council to make Solid Waste Management watch its waste contractors more closely. Its contract portfolio was over 300 contracts worth $1.8 billion. Contractors must answer 311 requests, share GPS truck data and file accurate daily reports.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1.8 billion.

title: Status of the Financial Statement Audits of the City’s Agencies and Corporations for the Year Ended December 31, 2025
topics: annual reports, audits, boards of management, financial reports, municipal services
brief: This is routine business. City Council receives the report on the status of the 2025 financial statement audits of the City's agencies, for information. No decision is needed.

title: Audit of the City's Administrative Penalty System for Parking and Red Light Camera Violations
topics: audits, parking, parking fines, penalties, red light cameras
brief: The Auditor General asks Council to have the City Solicitor cut the backlog of parking-ticket appeal reviews, with better online help for people fighting tickets and clearer time targets.

title: City of Toronto Audit Findings Report for the Year Ended December 31, 2025
topics: annual reports, audits, external services, finance (sc)
brief: This is routine business. KPMG presents its report on the audit of the City's 2025 financial statements. KPMG was appointed as the City's outside auditor in July 2025. No decision is needed.

title: Community Centres - 2025 Audited Financial Statements
topics: annual reports, audits, boards of management, community centres, financial reports
brief: This is routine business. City Council receives the 2025 audited financial statements for the 10 City community centres, for information. No decision is needed.

title: Arenas - 2025 Audited Financial Statements and Status of Outstanding 2025 Audited Financial Statements
topics: annual reports, arenas, audits, boards of management, financial reports
brief: This is routine business. City Council receives the 2025 audited financial statements for five City arenas, plus an update on the three audits still underway, for information. No decision is needed.

title: 1891 Eglinton Avenue East - Class 4 Noise Area Classification (NPC-300) - Final Report
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council can classify part of 1891 Eglinton Avenue East as a noise area. That step is needed before the planned mixed-use development can go ahead.

title: Public Health Role in Indoor Air Quality
brief: The board considers Toronto Public Health's role on indoor air quality, with recommendations for better public messaging, school board collaboration, and asking the province for help with wildfire smoke.

title: TTC St. Clair West Station - Sanitary Sewer Structural Lining Cost Recovery Agreement
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, fire hazards, sanitary sewers
brief: This is a procedural item: Council is asked to let Toronto Water make the TTC pay the full cost of sewer structural lining work near St. Clair West Station.

title: 3718 and 3730 Kingston Road - Zoning By-law Amendment - Appeal Report
brief: The developer behind 3718 and 3730 Kingston Road appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal after the city missed its decision deadline. Staff had recommended a 24-storey building with 419 homes.

title: 53 Strachan Avenue (Entrance Address 805 Wellington Street West) - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property, Demolition of Heritage Attributes and of a Building under Sections 33, 34(1)1 and 34(1)2 of the Ontario Heritage Act and Authority to Enter into a Heritage Easement Agreement
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve changes and partial demolition at Strachan House, a City-owned 1888 former planing mill at 53 Strachan Avenue, and demolition of a building at 805 Wellington Street West.

title: Lower Don Parkland Indigenous Naming - Progress Update
brief: Whether to have staff continue an Indigenous-led naming process with the Mississaugas of the Credit First Nation and report back in mid-2027 with a chosen Anishinaabemowin name for the Lower Don parkland system and trail now sits with Council.

title: 39 Wynford Drive - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: City Council plans to designate the property at 39 Wynford Drive in Flemingdon Park as a heritage property.

title: 55 Elm Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: City Council plans to designate the 1891 building at 55 Elm Street, built for the Canadian Temperance League, as a heritage property.

title: Considerations for Toronto Membership in the Association francophone des Municipalités de l'Ontario
brief: It's Council's call whether to have the City Manager register one staff member for membership in the Association francophone des municipalites de l'Ontario for 2026 and up to four memberships for 2027, and to ask councillors about interest in appointment.

title: Authority to Enter into an Extended Agreement with Parkrun Canada for Nominal Permits to Hold a Community Running Program
topics: permit renewal, tenancy agreements, walking tracks
brief: Extending the nominal-fee permit for Parkrun Canada's free weekly 5 km run/walk on the Martin Goodman Trail. It goes to Council for approval.

title: Toronto Fire Services 2025 Annual Report
topics: annual reports, fire and rescue services
brief: Council got the Toronto Fire Services 2025 annual report. Council asked staff to study how provincial rule changes affect fire service costs, and told the City Manager to negotiate with the province to recover those costs. Staff must also report back on improving fire response times in Etobicoke, Scarborough and Don Valley.
stake: About annual reports. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 25 in favour, none against.

title: 32 Bright Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: City Council plans to designate Costigan Cottage, a wood-frame worker's cottage at 32 Bright Street in Corktown, as a heritage property.

title: 55 Sudbury Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: City Council plans to designate the property at 55 Sudbury Street in Little Portugal as a heritage property.

title: 180 Queens Drive - Proposed Designation By-law Under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
brief: City Council will decide whether to go ahead with designating 180 Queens Drive as a heritage property despite the owner's objection.

title: 6278 Kingston Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: City Council plans to designate the John Morrish House at 6278 Kingston Road in Scarborough as a heritage property.

title: 2 Hedgewood Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: City Council plans to designate the property at 2 Hedgewood Road, near the West Don River Valley, as a heritage property.
stake: About heritage designation. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Ookwemin Minising - Draft Plan of Subdivision Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: This is a routine item: council is being told the Development Review head plans to approve the subdivision plan for Ookwemin Minising under delegated authority. No council decision is required.

title: Amendments to the Policy for Accepting Potentially Contaminated Lands to be Conveyed to the City under the Planning Act
topics: contaminated soil, environmental policies, planning & development (sc)
brief: This is a procedural item: Council is asked to update the policy for accepting potentially contaminated lands conveyed to the city through development approvals.

title: 235 and 245 Yorkland Boulevard - Official Plan Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will decide whether to redesignate 235 and 245 Yorkland Boulevard from employment to mixed-use, with a new public road, park, and affordable housing secured.
stake: Ward 17 is named in the record.

title: Auditor General's 2026 Consolidated Follow-up Report Status of Outstanding Recommendations for City Divisions, Agencies and Corporations
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, annual reports, audits, parking authorities, police services
brief: Receiving the Auditor General's 2026 follow-up report on unfinished recommendations. It goes to City Council for a decision. A private document stays secret because it covers City property security.

title: Traffic Control Signals and Turn Prohibitions - Victoria Park Avenue and Wakehood Street
topics: traffic control systems, transportation, turn prohibitions (traffic)
brief: Approving traffic signals at Victoria Park and Wakehood Street, plus bans on some through and left-turn movements. It goes to Council for approval.

title: Continuous Controls Monitoring: City Staff Overtime, Absenteeism, and Other Payroll-Related Expenses
topics: audits, employees, human resources, labour force, payment, sick leave
brief: The Auditor General asks Council to have the Chief People Officer review the City's 2001 attendance program and strengthen oversight. Overtime rose from $109.3 million to $134.1 million and paid sick leave from $109.2 million to $131.9 million between 2023 and 2025; workers earning over $50,000 in overtime were flagged.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $50,000.

title: Follow Up on 2026.EC27.1: Refining the Definition of an Entertainment Establishment/Nightclub in Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 545, Licensing
topics: business licences, entertainment establishments, municipal codes, nightclubs
brief: Council will weigh whether to amend the licensing by-law so that venues with a capacity under 151 people are not classed as nightclubs, and are instead licensed based on what they actually do.

title: Call to Order
brief: City Council opens its meeting with O Canada and a moment of silence.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: City Council confirms the minutes from its June 24 and 25, 2026 meeting.

title: Improving the Usability of Old City Hall as a Filming Location
topics: film and television industry, film permits
brief: It's the committee's call whether to have staff review fees, accessibility and operating conditions for film and TV production at Old City Hall, consult industry stakeholders, and report in 2027 on actions to cut costs and improve usability.

title: Toronto Water 2026 Capital Budget and 2027 to 2035 Capital Plan Adjustments
brief: The decision on whether to move $32.683 million between Toronto Water capital projects to speed up some and delay others, with no change to the total budget rests with Council. Two projects also get a $245.294 million cost increase so contracts can be awarded ahead of schedule.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Bloomberg Finance LP for the Provision of Continued Leasing Proprietary Software and Data Services
topics: agreements, contracts, leasing, science & technology (sc), software
brief: Approving a no-bid 1-year $392,400 USD ($399,306 USD net of HST recoveries) Bloomberg financial data deal, with 3 renewal options. It goes to City Council for approval. A $500,000 figure is also cited.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $392,400.

title: Property Taxes: 2027 Interim Levy By-Law
brief: Council decides whether to approve a 2027 interim property tax bill of about $3.13 billion, half of 2026 taxes, to keep the city funded until the 2027 budget passes.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $3.13 billion.

title: Ombudsman Toronto Report - No Refunds for Discontinued TTC Tickets and Tokens: An Investigation Behind How the Decision was Made
brief: The Ombudsman asks council to accept his report on how the TTC decided not to refund or credit discontinued old tickets and tokens. It makes eight suggestions the TTC has agreed to put in place.

title: 2026 Heads and Beds Levy on Institutions
brief: Before Council for a decision: set the 2026 tax of $75 per bed or student on colleges, universities, hospitals, and jails, expected to raise about $20.6 million. Indexed to inflation the rate would be $186.08, worth an extra $30.6 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $20.6 million.

title: 1113-1125 Dundas Street West - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, parking machines, parking regulations, stopping prohibitions, transportation
parking bylaws, pay and display machines
brief: City Council will decide whether to close the south sidewalk and part of Dundas Street West east of Ossington Avenue for 24 months (September 2026 to September 2028) while a 10-storey affordable housing building is built. Five parking spots will be removed and the builder will pay the lost parking revenue at $4.50.

title: Capital Variance Report for the Twelve Months Ended December 31, 2025
brief: Approving mid-year changes to the 2025-2034 capital budget to match year-end funding needs, after 2025 capital spending of $5.603 billion, up from $4.740 billion in 2024 goes to Council for a decision. One attachment stays private over a land deal.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $5.603 billion.

title: Advancing More Supportive Housing to Address Homelessness and Create Pathways to Long-Term Housing Stability
brief: A committee asks council to press Ontario and the federal government for steady, long-term funding for supportive housing for people leaving homelessness.
stake: About homelessness. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: 18 Great Oak Drive - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: City Council plans to designate the Moore Farmhouse at 18 Great Oak Drive in Etobicoke as a heritage property.

title: Amending the Composition of the City's Appointments to the Toronto Pan Am Sports Centre Board of Directors
topics: boards of management, public appointments, special purpose bodies
brief: Changing one of its five seats on the Toronto Pan Am Sports Centre board from a director-level to a manager-level city staff member heads to Council for a decision.

title: Chin Radio Building - Loading Zone
brief: The community council will decide whether to change parking rules in front of the CHIN Radio building at 622 College Street to add passenger pick-up and drop-off space.

title: Obligatory Reserve Funds, Reserves and Discretionary Reserve Funds as at December 31, 2025
topics: budgets and accounts, reserves and reserve funds
brief: Creating a reserve fund to pay for replacing vehicles and equipment used by the environment and forestry division heads to Council for a decision. The report lists reserve balances: $6,726.4 million, $6,597.5 million, $128.9 million, $2,840.2, $2,466.5 million, $373.7 million, $5,612.8 million, $5,471.2 million, $141.6 million, $5,131.6 million, $339.6 million, $18,863.7 million, $44,349.1 million, $12,068.7 million, and $12.6 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $6,726.4 million.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports, New Business and Business Previously Requested from City Officials
brief: City Council formally introduces the committee reports it will consider at this meeting.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: Council members declare any conflicts of interest under provincial law.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Petitions
brief: Council members may file petitions.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: Various presentations and announcements are made at the council meeting.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: City Council reviews the Order Paper listing its business.
stake: A citywide decision. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 25 in favour, none against.

title: 2026 Levy on Railway Roadways and Rights-of-Way and on Power Utility Transmission and Distribution Corridors
brief: The decision on whether to approve the 2026 tax on railway and power corridor lands, totalling $6,993,742 ($6,484,859 municipal, $508,883 education), at the same rates as the 2025 total of $6,992,485 ($6,483,956 municipal, $508,529 education) rests with Council. Indexed to inflation it would raise an extra $3,891,024; the report's figures also include $3,601,155.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $6,993,742.

title: Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation Annual General Meeting and 2025 Audited Financial Statements
brief: This is a routine item: council holds the Toronto Seniors Housing Corporation's yearly shareholder meeting and reviews its 2025 reports. Nothing changes.

title: Site Plan Application Fee Review
brief: City Council will decide whether to update the fee schedule for Site Plan Control applications, following a review of the site plan process.

title: Indigenous Women and Children’s Shelter, 68 Sheppard Avenue West
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng (Ward 18) filed an inquiry asking city staff to publicly clarify key facts about the planned Indigenous Women and Children's Shelter at 68 Sheppard Avenue West.
stake: About urban planning. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Leitner-Poma Canada Inc., for the Supply and Maintenance of the Ski Lifts at Earl Bales Ski and Snowboard Centre and Rope Tow Lift at Don Valley Golf Course for Parks and Recreation
topics: contracts, golf courses, parks, ski centres, suppliers
brief: Approving a no-bid $418,363 ($425,726 net of HST recoveries) deal with Leitner-Poma for ski lift parts and maintenance at Earl Bales and Don Valley. It goes to City Council for approval. A $500,000 figure is also cited.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $418,363.

title: Community Space Tenancy Lease Agreement with WoodGreen Community Services - 90 Mill Street and 373 Front Street East
topics: community & life (sc), leasing, properties (real estate), tenants
brief: Approving leasing about 5,015 square feet at 90 Mill Street and 373 Front Street East to WoodGreen Community Services for community programs. It goes to City Council for approval.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Kemira Water Solutions Canada Inc., for the Supply of Iron Salts at Wastewater Treatment Plants for Toronto Water
topics: contracts, sewer and water infrastructure, suppliers, wastewater treatment plants
waste water treatment plants, sewer and water services
brief: Approving a no-bid 1-year $43,484,155 ($44,249,476 net of HST recoveries) deal with Kemira for iron salts that strip phosphorus at the city's four wastewater plants. It goes to City Council for approval. A $500,000 figure is also cited.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $43,484,155.

title: Non-Competitive Contracts with Suppliers for the Supply of Proprietary Parts and Maintenance Services at Water and Wastewater Treatment Plants for Toronto Water
topics: contracts, sewer and water infrastructure, suppliers, water treatment plants
water treatment facilities, sewer and water services
brief: Approving two no-bid deals totalling $1,368,432, ($1,392,517 net of HST recoveries): $368,432 ($374,917) with Johnson Controls and $1,000,000 ($1,017,600) with Lakeside Process Controls, for proprietary water plant parts. It goes to City Council for approval. $500,000 and $1,368,432 are also cited.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1,368,432.

title: Litigation Arising from Baycrest Park Revitalization Phase 1
topics: damages, insurance claims, legal matters, parks, projects
brief: The city fired its Baycrest Park builder in 2024, says the insurer wrongly denied its bond claim, and is now suing. Council is asked to adopt confidential legal instructions.

title: Non-Competitive Contracts with Jenoptik Smart Mobility Solutions, LLC for Red-Light Camera Systems
topics: contracts, red light cameras, road safety, science & technology (sc)

topics: donation, finance (sc), long term care homes, seniors housing
toy drive, homes for the aged

stake: The official summary names a figure of $0.800 million.

brief: The community council will decide whether to reopen its March 2026 refusal of a sidewalk encroachment at 666 Spadina Avenue, after the councillor negotiated a settlement with the developer.

brief: This is a routine item: council is asked to receive an update on the June 2026 national municipal conference in Edmonton. Nothing changes.

brief: Approving a 5-year nominal lease with Birchmount Bluffs Neighbourhood Centre at 93 Birchmount Road, where it has run programs since 1994. It goes to City Council for approval.

brief: The community council will decide whether to keep Metrolinx Exhibition Station construction trucks off Strachan Avenue and Liberty Village neighbourhood streets.

topics: contracts, digital libraries, information and communication technology, purchasing
brief: Adding $233,620 USD ($322,395 CAD), or $237,731 USD ($328,069 CAD) net of HST, to the Medallia survey tool deal for 2026-2027. It goes to City Council for a decision. Also cited: $195,364, $428,983, $1, and $1.38.

stake: The official summary names a figure of $3,754,157.

title: Improving Permit Parking on Old Weston Road
topics: parking prohibitions, parking regulations, permit parking
brief: The community council will decide whether to add permit parking on the east side of Old Weston Road between Davenport Road and St. Clair Avenue West, creating about 25 spaces.

brief: This is a routine item: council holds Build Toronto's yearly shareholder meeting, reviews its 2025 reports, and appoints its 2026 auditor. Nothing changes.

brief: This is a routine item: council holds the Toronto Port Lands Company's yearly shareholder meeting, reviews its 2025 reports, and appoints its 2026 auditor. Nothing changes.

brief: This is a procedural item: City Council is asked to update the records retention by-law by deleting the Auditor General audit records category, now covered elsewhere.

brief: The community council will decide whether to add an accessible loading zone on Queen Street West east of Walnut Avenue for a Wheel-Trans user's household, removing two metered spots.

brief: The city wants to extend its e-Builder project-management platform deal 4 years and add new orders. Figures cited: an amendment of $4,988,313 ($5,076,107), from $5,968,061 to $10,956,374, plus new orders of $2,068,401 ($2,104,805) and $1,049,928 ($1,068,407).

topics: animal services, contracts, information and communication technology, licences, pets
brief: Approving changes to the DocuPet pet licensing deal, first set at $680,730 for 5 years with a possible $1,537,136 ($1,756,072 net of HST recoveries) total. brief: City Council will decide whether to close Yorkville Avenue from September 8 to 14, 2026, for an expanded Rogers-sponsored TIFF red-carpet event that needs more than the usual four days.

topics: community centres, legal aid, legal matters
community complexes, legal assistance, legal issues
brief: Council decides whether to let The 519 community centre give limited legal advice to eligible 2SLGBTQ+ community members, with safety and accountability rules.

topics: loading zones, parking prohibitions, permit parking
pick up zones, no parking, on-street permit parking
brief: City Council will decide whether to add an accessible loading zone in front of the new community centre on the Davisville school site, for Wheel-Trans vehicles and permit holders.

brief: This is a routine item: council reviews the Toronto Pan Am Sports Centre's 2025 audited reports and reappoints its auditor. Nothing changes.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
brief: This is routine business. City Council will introduce general bills and confirming bills, the formal by-laws that enact Council's decisions as law.
stake: About by-laws. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 22 in favour, none against.

title: Endorsement of the Council of Chief Medical Officers of Health Position Statement on Digital Culture and Child and Youth Well-Being
brief: Endorsing a national chief medical officers' statement calling for a precautionary approach to social media and smartphones for children and youth. It goes to the Board of Health for approval.

title: Follow-up on Item 2026.MM42.61: Suitability of the Standard Theatre as a Live Music Venue
brief: This is for information only: council receives a report finding that turning the vacant Standard Theatre at 285 Spadina Avenue, which opened in 1921 for Yiddish theatre, into a live music venue would be allowed. No policy change is proposed.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Protective Tree Fencing in Yorkville Village - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
brief: Releasing $218,906 plus tax ($247,363 in total) for protective tree fencing around 119 Yorkville tree pits. It goes to Council for approval.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $218,906.

title: 49 Thorncliffe Park Drive, 1707 - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number: 26 145743 PRS 00 IV
brief: This is a procedural item: the owner of 49 Thorncliffe Park Drive, 1707 is appealing a property standards order issued April 17, 2026 before the Property Standards Committee.

brief: This is a procedural item: an appeal of a property standards order for 57 John Perkins Bull Drive,2 (issued March 26, 2026) goes to the Property Standards Committee.

brief: Recommending two public members and a Chair for the Sankofa Square Board, plus two members picked by the local business group. It goes to the Civic Appointments Committee for a decision.

title: Arena Boards of Management Settlement of Operating Results for the Year Ended 2024
brief: Up for a decision before Council: send $204,163 in surpluses from three arenas to the city to help cover $201,746 in shortfalls at four other arenas. The report's figures also include $2,417 and $210,055.

title: Lakeshore Arena Corporation - Annual General Meeting and 2025 Audited Financial Statements
brief: This is a routine item: council holds Lakeshore Arena's yearly shareholder meeting, reviews its 2025 reports, and appoints its 2026 auditor. Nothing changes.

title: Association of Community Centres Settlement of Operating Results for Year Ended 2024 and 2025
brief: Council is set to decide whether to send $118,971 in surpluses from four community centres to the city to help cover $406,589 in shortfalls at six other centres. The report's figures also include $287,618, $203,621, $105,737, and $97,884.

title: Capital Variance Report for the Four Months Ended April 30, 2026
brief: The decision on whether to approve mid-year changes to the 2026-2035 capital budget, plus a report on 2026 capital spending of $1.106 billion through April 30 rests with Council. Total capital spending is projected to reach $5.417 billion by year-end, 89.9 per cent of the approved capital budget.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1.106 billion.

title: Ontario Place Construction Management Plan for Pedestrian and Cycling Safety and Traffic Management
brief: The community council will consider requiring a construction management plan for the Ontario Place redevelopment, after the province skipped the city's usual approval process.

brief: City Council can approve traffic signals at Pharmacy Avenue and Stamford Square South/Rosita Crescent. Residents raised concerns about crossing safely.

title: Toronto Community Housing Corporation - Annual General Meeting and 2025 Audited Consolidated Financial Statements
brief: Council held Toronto Community Housing's yearly shareholder meeting, reviewed its 2025 reports, and appointed its 2026 auditor. Council also asked for a plan to expand deep building repairs that protect tenants from extreme heat, to be reported on in the 2027 budget process.

title: 701 Fleet Street - Authorization to Enter into a Long-term Lease and Community Access Agreement with Tempo Basketball Club Inc.
brief: The call on whether to approve a 40-year lease for a new women's pro basketball practice facility at 701 Fleet Street, with a public park, outdoor courts, and year-round public access belongs to Council. The report cites $0.8 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $0.8 million. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 22 in favour, none against.

title: Operating Variance Report for the Year Ended December 31, 2025
brief: Approving changes to the 2025 operating budget with no net impact goes to Council for a decision. The city's tax-funded operations ended 2025 $108.2 million under budget, and rate-supported programs $66.1 million under.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $108.2 million.

title: Operating Variance Report for the Four Months Ended April 30, 2026
brief: The call on whether to approve changes to the 2026 operating budget with no net impact, plus a report on results through April 30 showing a $4.6 million unfavourable variance and a projected $97.4 million year-end variance belongs to Council. The report's figures also include $27.7 million and $32.7 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $4.6 million.

title: Advancing Work on Bremner Boulevard Pedestrian Safety Improvements
brief: The community council will decide whether to advance pedestrian safety work on Bremner Boulevard near the CN Tower, where staff are studying crosswalk options.

brief: This is routine business: the City's lawyer asks council for direction on a hearing about the Pier 27 phase three waterfront project at 19 to 37 Queens Quay East, with 45- and 11-storey buildings, which council refused. Details stay private as legal advice.
stake: About appeals. Council sent it back for more work.

stake: The official summary names a figure of $306,000.

brief: Releasing $336,979 for Elm Street streetscape work by the Downtown Yonge BIA. It goes to Council for approval.

brief: Studying the Sneaky Dee's building at 431 College Street for heritage protection after its demolition bid was withdrawn. It goes to Council for a decision.

brief: City Council will consider an infrastructure reimbursement and budget update for phases two and three of the Lawrence Heights revitalization by Toronto Community Housing.

brief: Proclaiming July as Caribbean Heritage Month, noting the Carnival's $467 million to $532 million economic impact. It goes to Council for approval.

brief: Exploring year-round use of seasonal recreation spaces like ice pads in the off-season. It goes to Council for a decision.

brief: A councillor wants the Planning and Housing Committee to back asking the province to protect listed heritage properties whose register protection expires December 31, 2026.

brief: This is routine business: the City's lawyer asks council how to handle a hearing about a proposed 29-storey mixed-use building with 423 homes at 2915 to 2943 Bloor Street West. Details stay private as legal advice.

brief: This is routine business: the City's lawyer asks council how to handle remaining appeals of the land-use change that added 283 kilometres of new Avenues, ahead of a November 2026 hearing. Details stay private as legal advice.

brief: This is just for information: council receives the Integrity Commissioner's 2025 annual report. No decision is needed.

brief: This is just for information: council receives a report answering its request for a ward-based maintenance crew pilot, describing the City's current area-based approach and what study would be needed first. No decision is needed.

title: Exploring Partnerships to Create a New Community Centre with Toronto's Filipino Community - by Councillor Neethan Shan, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: Exploring partnerships to build a permanent Filipino cultural and community centre, using the Chinese Cultural Centre and Tamil Community Centre as models. It goes to City Council for a decision. More than 270,000 Toronto residents are of Filipino origin, and Scarborough's Filipino community has no dedicated facility.
stake: About community centres. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 24 in favour, none against.

brief: This is routine business: the City's lawyer asks council how to handle a hearing about a proposed 43-storey building with 442 homes at 1410 to 1416 Eglinton Avenue West. Details stay private as legal advice.
stake: About zoning bylaws. Decided by a recorded vote, 23 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

brief: This is routine business: the City's lawyer asks council how to handle a hearing about a proposed 30-storey building at 15 to 17 Elm Street, including a heritage designation appeal. Details stay private as legal advice.

brief: This is routine business: the City's lawyer asks council whether to agree to let the owner of 110 to 112 Adelaide Street East ask the land-dispute board to review its 2026 decision, to advance a revised proposal. Details stay private as legal advice.

brief: This is routine business: the City's lawyer asks council how to handle a hearing starting November 30, 2026 about a proposed 55-storey building at 147 to 151 Liberty Street. Details stay private as legal advice.

brief: This is routine business: the City's lawyer asks council for direction on a hearing about a proposed 46-storey purpose-built rental building at 30 to 36 Hendon Avenue, which council refused. Details stay private as legal advice.

brief: This is routine business: the City's lawyer asks council how to handle an ongoing hearing about proposed 37- and 35-storey towers at 245 to 251 Marlee Avenue, which council opposes. Details stay private as legal advice.
stake: About zoning bylaws. Decided by a recorded vote, 20 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

brief: This is routine business: the City's lawyer asks council how to handle a hearing about a proposed 24-storey mixed-use building with 256 homes at 237 Victoria Street. Details stay private as legal advice.

title: Renew Sheppard East Secondary Plan - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: This is routine business: the City's lawyer asks council how to handle seventeen landowner appeals of the Renew Sheppard East Secondary Plan land-use rules. Details stay private as legal advice.

brief: This is just for information: council receives a status update on Canada Post's switch to community mailboxes in Toronto, including answers to council's questions. No decision is needed.

title: Addressing Moribund Development Sites - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: Developing tools for stalled development sites that sit vacant while neighbours deal with the fallout. It goes to Council for a decision.

brief: This is routine business: council gives senior City staff temporary decision-making power during the 2026 election break so City business keeps running after the current term ends. The authority thresholds are $5 million, $10 million, $2 million, $50,000, $500,000, $100,000 and $50 million.

title: 743 Warden Avenue - Amending Section 37 Agreement for Blocks 6, 7 and 8 Plan 66M-2549 - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
brief: Procedural: council is asked to amend the Section 37 deal for Blocks 6-8 of the 743 Warden Avenue townhouse development.

title: Securing A Permanent Facility for the Central Eglinton Community Centre - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: Securing a permanent home for the Central Eglinton Community Centre at 160 Eglinton Avenue East. It goes to Council for a decision.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Toronto Community Housing for Cooling Upgrades at 275 Shuter Street - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: Releasing $150,000 for cooling upgrades to the community room at 275 Shuter Street. It goes to Council for approval.

title: Enhancing Tenant Safety Through a Review of Toronto Community Housing Corporation CCTV Camera Coverage, Visitor Verification Measures and Related Policies - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher

brief: Approving tearing down a non-heritage building at 1337 Queen Street West and building a 16-storey replacement, as part of the city-led Parkdale Hub project expanding community services is on City Council's agenda.

brief: It's City Council's call whether to approve tearing down 7 rental homes at 143 and 147 Main Street, if the owner replaces them with 7 new rentals and gives tenants compensation and a right to return. The approval carries a $20,000.00 financial condition.

title: Realignment of Permit Parking Area 1E to Exclude the Development Located at 3459 and 3461 Dundas Street West
brief: The decision on removing the building at 3459 and 3461 Dundas Street West from Permit Parking Area 1E, so its residents would no longer qualify for overnight street parking permits rests with City Council.

title: 564-576 Sherbourne Street and 29-37 Linden Street - Rental Housing Demolition - Amending Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, development, rental housing, urban planning
brief: A decision on a revised plan to tear down 23 rentals at 564-576 Sherbourne Street and 29-37 Linden Street, replacing them with 25 rental units, and turning 23 rental rooms into 20 studios goes to City Council. The approval carries a $20,000.00 financial condition.

title: 914 Bathurst Street - Construction Staging Area
brief: Up for a decision before City Council: close the west sidewalk and southbound lane on Bathurst Street and part of Barton Avenue from May 2026 to November 2028, to build a 12-storey condo, with a temporary walkway. The report references a $2.00 fee amount.

title: 777 Victoria Park Avenue - Construction Staging Area
brief: City Council will decide whether to allow temporary road and sidewalk closures for construction at 777 Victoria Park Avenue.

title: 5, 7, 9 and 11 Bellamy Road South - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve 110 townhouses, mostly three- and four-bedroom, at 5-11 Bellamy Road South.

title: Metrolinx Eglinton Crosstown West Extension - Station Construction - Long-term Temporary Road Closures and Traffic By-law Amendments
topics: by-laws, change, road closures, temporary signs, traffic, urban transit systems
brief: To build three Eglinton Crosstown West light-rail stations, council is asked to approve long-term lane closures, temporary traffic lights, and detours for walkers and cyclists.

title: Hollyhock Court, Mattamy (North York) Limited - Assumption of Services, Registered Plan 66M-2567
topics: assumption of services, municipal services, properties (real estate), subdivision (land)
brief: Taking over the municipal services built for the Hollyhock Court subdivision and release the developer's guarantee. It goes to City Council for a decision.

title: 844 Don Mills Road and 1150 Eglinton Avenue East (Block 8) - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: development, exemptions, planning approvals, properties (real estate), townhouses
brief: Approving a legal step that lets eighty townhouses at 844 Don Mills Road and 1150 Eglinton Avenue East be sold as separate lots. It goes to City Council for approval.

topics: avenue study, planning, urban design, urban form, urban planning
brief: Approving a new planning vision for the Don Mills Regeneration Areas, turning employment lands into mixed-use communities near the Crosstown LRT. It goes to City Council for approval.

title: 1243 Islington Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: A builder wants a 61-storey tower with about 702 homes at 1243 Islington Avenue, plus a small public plaza. Council is asked to change the zoning to allow it.

brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie is asking City Council to rename part of Zoo Road 'Rouge National Urban Park Road.' The park is building a $20 million visitor centre set to open in 2027.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $20 million.

title: 555 Rexdale Boulevard - Woodbine Secondary Plan Study, Infrastructure Master Plan and Transportation Master Plan - Interim Report
topics: Master Plans, Secondary Plans, infrastructure, transportation
brief: Staff summarize a planning study for the southeast Woodbine lands so far. Council is asked to back the emerging ideas before more study and public input.

title: Proposed Humber Bay Shores Business Improvement Area Poll Results
brief: Council decides whether to designate the Humber Bay Shores area as a new Business Improvement Area, after a poll where most accepted ballots were in favour, and to have the City Solicitor prepare the designation by-law.

title: Changes to Business Improvement Area Board of Management
brief: This is an administrative item: council is asked to remove Tara Longo as a director of The Eglinton Way Business Improvement Area board of management.

title: 2673-2675 Bayview Avenue - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: construction, exemptions, planning, properties (real estate), townhouses
brief: Approving a legal step that lets ten townhouses at 2673-2675 Bayview Avenue be sold as separate lots. It goes to City Council for approval.

title: 7 St. Dennis Drive - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction permits (right-of-way), permits, road closures, street occupation permits
brief: Letting a builder close the south sidewalk, part of the bike lane and part of the traffic lane on St. Dennis Drive for 25 months, from September 2026 to September 2028, for a 37-storey building. It goes to City Council for a decision.

title: 2600 Don Mills Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Appeal Report
topics: construction, demolitions, planning & development (sc), residential properties, zoning bylaws
building, residential real estate, zoning by-laws
brief: An appeal report sets out the City's position on four tall buildings with 1,814 homes proposed at 2600 Don Mills Road, which would replace a 19-storey rental building with 226 units.

title: Ossington Avenue Safety and Streetscape Improvements
brief: City Council is set to decide whether to approve a redesign of Ossington Avenue between Dundas and Queen streets, with wider sidewalks, safer lanes and full-time parking, aimed at cutting crashes on the busy strip.

title: 5500 Dundas Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: A builder wants 14- and 16-storey towers with about 560 homes at 5500 Dundas Street West, plus shops and a plaza. Council is asked to change the zoning to allow it.

title: 3100 Weston Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: zoning bylaw amendments, residential real estate
brief: A builder proposed three 4-storey buildings with about 125 homes at 3100 Weston Road, then appealed after council missed the deadline. Staff want city lawyers to oppose the current version.

title: 75-81 Billy Bishop Way - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Appeal Report
topics: Official Plans, appeals, official plan amendments, planning, rezoning, urban planning, zoning bylaws
brief: An appeal report sets out the City's position on the proposal for five tall buildings with 2,055 homes at 75-81 Billy Bishop Way.
stake: About Official Plans. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 20 in favour, none against.

title: Lake Shore Boulevard West at Silver Moon Drive - Lane Designation
topics: activities in transportation, attributes in transportation
brief: Staff want the right eastbound lane on Lake Shore Boulevard West near Silver Moon Drive marked right-turn only, to reduce driver conflicts.

title: Black Creek Drive and Weston Road - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
brief: Staff recommend two pedestrian crossings where Black Creek Drive meets Weston Road, plus yield signs for drivers, to make crossing safer for walkers.

title: Humberline Drive and Claireville Drive (south intersection) - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
brief: Staff recommend traffic lights at Humberline Drive and Claireville Drive to make crossing safer for walkers. Crossings just north of the intersection would be banned.

title: 110-114 Maitland Street and 440 Jarvis Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Appeal Report
topics: appeals, rental housing, residential properties, zoning bylaws
rental units, residential real estate, zoning by-laws
brief: The builder of a 56-storey building at 110-114 Maitland Street appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal after council missed its deadline. Council is asked to have its lawyer oppose the appeal while talks continue.

title: 257, 259 and 291 Lake Shore Boulevard East, 2 Small Street and 200 Queens Quay East (Quayside Blocks 1 and 2) - Urban Design Guidelines - Final Report
topics: building plans, urban design, zoning bylaws
building records, civic improvements, zoning by-laws
brief: Whether to approve the urban design guidelines for Quayside Blocks 1 and 2 on the waterfront now sits with City Council. Approval is needed before the first building plan there can move ahead.

title: Liberty For All Regeneration Area Study - Final Report
topics: community development, employment opportunities, housing, official plan amendments
brief: It's City Council's call whether to adopt a new vision for Liberty Village's growth as a transit-friendly community with homes and jobs. It tackles traffic, requires more trees and affordable housing from new buildings, and expands roads.

title: 50 Richmond Street East - Construction Staging Area
brief: City Council has the final say on whether to close the north sidewalk on Richmond Street East from June 2026 to July 2027, for interior work at 50 Richmond Street East. A shared walkway and bike lane would be set up.

title: 1215 to 1255 McCowan Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Refusal
brief: Staff recommend refusing a plan for three tall towers with 1,412 homes at 1215 to 1255 McCowan Road. City Council will decide.

title: Guildwood Village Neighbourhood Character Guidelines
brief: Design guidelines for the Guildwood Village area would set the look and character of future development there. City Council is asked to adopt them.

title: Ellesmere Road and Crocus Drive/Dewey Drive - Traffic Control Signals
brief: Staff checked a request for traffic signals at Ellesmere Road and Crocus Drive/Dewey Drive and found the rules were not met. City Council is asked not to approve them.

title: Kingston Road and Blantyre Avenue - Traffic Control Signals and Parking Amendments
topics: change, traffic control systems, traffic signals
brief: Traffic signals would go up at Kingston Road and Blantyre Avenue, with the nearby pedestrian island removed. Staff say signals would protect walkers better, even though the usual rules were not met. City Council is asked to approve. A related parking change adjusts the $3.25-per-hour pay-and-display rules on Kingston Road.

title: 206 Russell Hill Road - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Up for a decision before City Council: exempt 206 Russell Hill Road from lot-division rules for three years, so the property can be split into four home lots sharing underground parking.

title: 235 Wicksteed Avenue - Temporary Use Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Allowing a temporary concrete batching plant and office trailer at 235 Wicksteed Avenue for up to three years. It goes to City Council for a decision.

title: Use of Nathan Phillips Square for Various Events - October 1, 2026 - April 30, 2027
brief: Whether to grant exceptions so eight events — including festivals — can use Nathan Phillips Square from October 2026 to April 2027, with some allowed to serve beer and wine under rules now sits with City Council.

title: 307 Sherbourne Street - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
topics: community safety, construction, sidewalks, traffic regulations
brief: The decision on extending the construction closure on Sherbourne Street's east sidewalk and bike lane from June 2026 to January 2027, for an 18-storey student residence rests with City Council.

title: 1650 Military Trail (Phase 1) - Construction Staging Area
brief: City Council will decide whether to allow road closures on Morrish Road for construction of an 8-storey student rental building at 1650 Military Trail.

title: 374-390 Dupont Street - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning
brief: A decision on approving growing the project at 374-390 Dupont Street from 12 to 16 storeys, while shrinking the shop space sits with City Council. A city plan change is needed for the extra height.

title: Bellamy Road North and Danforth Road - Traffic Safety Improvements
brief: Road safety changes at Bellamy Road North and Danforth Road, following a study of speeding and walker safety in the Eglinton-Bendale South area, go to City Council for approval.

title: 468 to 480 Danforth Road and 509 Birchmount Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve a 14-storey building with 526 homes and ground-floor shops at 468 to 480 Danforth Road and 509 Birchmount Road. The plan would also expand the nearby Sadler Parkette.

title: Temporary Adjustments to Permit Parking Relocation on Mathersfield Drive and Chestnut Park
brief: The decision on whether to allow temporary permit parking on Mathersfield Drive and Chestnut Park for about a year starting June 2026, replacing street parking lost to watermain work nearby rests with City Council.

title: 143, 145 and 147 Main Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning
brief: Approving a 10-storey building with 56 homes at 143-147 Main Street, including 7 replacement rental units for existing tenants heads to City Council for a decision.

title: 1095-1111 Danforth Avenue and 1117 Danforth Avenue - Construction Staging Area
brief: Before City Council for a decision: close the south sidewalk, bike lane and parking lane on Danforth Avenue from June 2026 to April 2029, to build a 14-storey rental apartment, with temporary walkway and bike lanes. The $3.25-per-hour parking spaces would be temporarily removed.

title: Orton Park Road - Parking and Traffic Amendments
brief: U-turns and some left turns would be banned in front of George B. Little Public School on Orton Park Road. Staff say the changes would make drop-off and pick-up safer. City Council is asked to approve.

title: Accessible Parking Space - Davenport Road (Non-Delegated)
brief: City Council is set to decide whether to add a new accessible parking spot on Davenport Road east of Dufferin Street, and to remove an older marked spot near Bartlett Avenue that is no longer needed.

title: 1, 2A and 4-16 Sumach Street and 90 Eastern Avenue - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: planning & development (sc), residential properties, zoning bylaws
brief: Approving two tall towers at Sumach Street and Eastern Avenue: a 59-storey mixed-use building and a 55-storey residential building with 1,276 homes plus shops comes before City Council.

title: Formerly 95 Pidgeon Street (Blocks 1-3 of Plan 66M-2562) - Part Lot Control Exemption Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will decide whether to exempt 95 Pidgeon Street from part lot control rules. That would allow 26 three-storey townhouses to be built.

title: High Park Avenue - Parking Amendments
brief: Changing parking rules on High Park Avenue so permit holders can no longer block the daycare's short pickup zone at High Park Early Learning Centre on weekday afternoons is on City Council's agenda.

title: Oakwood Village Streets Plan - Non-Delegated Road Safety Improvements
brief: The decision on whether to approve Oakwood Village road safety changes: a new pedestrian light at Oakwood and Clovelly, removal of an old crosswalk, and weekday morning and afternoon turn bans at Oakwood and Earnscliffe rests with City Council.

title: 291 Lake Shore Boulevard East, 2 Small Street and 200 Queens Quay East (Quayside Blocks 1B, 1C and 2) - City-initiated Zoning By-law Amendments - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Approving city-led zoning changes for Quayside Blocks 1B, 1C and 2 to allow a new Toronto Public Library branch on the waterfront, plus small technical fixes goes to City Council for a decision.

title: Transit Priority Measures to Support Transit Diversions during the College Street / Carlton Street Closure Between Bay Street and Church Street
topics: road closures, traffic regulations, transportation, turn prohibitions (traffic)
brief: A decision on temporary parking and traffic changes so the 506 Carlton streetcar can be rerouted while College and Carlton streets close for sewer and track work from late July to December 2026 goes to City Council.

title: Housing Action Plan: Incorporating Low-rise Residential Lands into Zoning By-law 569-2013 -   Scarborough District - Final Report
brief: City Council will decide whether to bring low-rise residential areas in Scarborough into the city-wide zoning by-law, a cleanup step meant to simplify rules and support more housing.

title: Toronto Builds: 40 Bushby Drive - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve three residential towers of 44 to 59 storeys at 40 Bushby Drive in Scarborough, with at least 1,000 square metres of non-residential space.

title: Administrative Penalty Tribunal - Chair's 2025 Annual Report
brief: This is an information item: City Council is asked to receive the 2025 report from the chair of the tribunal that gives the final word on parking ticket disputes.

title: Achieving Universal Student Nutrition - 2026 Service Subsidies
brief: Sending $31.170 million in school nutrition funding — $7.216 million to the Angel Foundation and $23.954 million to the Toronto Foundation for Student Success — to finish a universal morning meal program in all public schools by 2026-2027. It goes to City Council for a decision.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $31.170 million.

title: Zoning for Low-Carbon Technologies - Final Report
brief: City Council will decide whether to update zoning to make it easier to install heat pumps, solar panels, energy storage, and electric vehicle chargers, supporting the city's 2040 net zero goal.

title: 1652 Keele Street - Community Space Tenancy Lease Agreement with The Black Women's Institute for Health and Municipal Capital Facility Designation
topics: city-owned properties, community associations, community centres, leasing
brief: Leasing about 2,017 square feet in the Keele Community Hub to The Black Women's Institute for Health and make the space tax-exempt. It goes to City Council for approval.

title: 1141 Bloor Street West and 980 Dufferin Street - Community Space Tenancy Lease Agreements and Municipal Capital Facility Designations for Five Tenant Agencies in the Bloor-Dufferin Community Hub
topics: city-owned properties, community centres, leasing, municipal facilities, non-profit organizations
brief: Leasing about 19,132 square feet in the Bloor-Dufferin Community Hub to five non-profits and make their spaces tax-exempt. It goes to City Council for approval.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with RouteSmart Technologies Inc., for the Continued Use of Collection Route Management and Service Planning Software for Solid Waste Management Services
topics: contracts, science & technology (sc), software, solid waste management
computer programs, solid waste management planning
brief: Approving a no-bid $850,000 ($864,960 net of HST recoveries) deal with RouteSmart for up to 5 years to move garbage route-planning software to the cloud after the vendor ended support for the old version. It goes to City Council for approval.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $850,000.

title: Delegation of Authority for Licence Agreements to Facilitate the use of Published Sound Recordings in Recreation Facilities
topics: audio recording, licences, music, recreational facilities
brief: Letting the Parks GM sign standing music licences with Re:Sound and SOCAN for recreation facilities. It goes to City Council for a decision. $80,000 in licensing costs is cited.
