topics: bridges, construction, legal matters, projects, watermains
brief: The city is suing its bridge watermain designer Parsons Inc., saying design errors stalled the Kipling Avenue Bridge project over the Humber River and raised costs. Council is asked to adopt confidential legal instructions.

title: Occupational Health and Safety Report: End of Year 2025
topics: employment & labour (sc), health (sc), injuries, working conditions
brief: This is an information item: the city's 2025 workplace safety report shows lost-time injuries up 7.5%, while WSIB costs fell from $65.95 million to $64.06 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $65.95 million.

title: Non-Competitive Bridge Contract with Arcadis Professional Services (Canada) Inc., for the Provision of the City’s Congestion Management Centre Operations Services
brief: Approving a $4,512,329 ($4,591,746 net of HST recoveries) no-bid 1-year deal with Arcadis to keep running the city's traffic management centre. It goes to City Council for approval. A $500,000 figure is also cited.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $4,512,329.

title: Award of Doc5398199635 to Alberici Constructors Ltd., for the New Ultraviolet Disinfection and Residuals Management Facility at the Island Water Treatment Plant, and Amendment to Purchase Orders 6056811 and 6057463 with AECOM Canada ULC for Contract Administration and Post-Construction Services
topics: contracts, projects, purchasing, wastewater treatment plants
brief: The city wants to give Alberici Constructors a $333,856,566 deal ($339,732,442 net of HST recoveries; stated as $333,856,56 in the report) for a new UV disinfection facility at the Island water plant, shift $99,966,862 in the water budget, and add $16,368,760 ($16,656,850) and $64,359 ($65,492) to two AECOM deals. Also cited: $3,724,823 ($3,790,380), $20,093,583 ($20,447,230), $275,435 ($280,283), and $339,794 ($345,775).
stake: The official summary names a figure of $333,856,56.

title: Non-Competitive Contracts for the Provision of the City’s Traffic Electrical Maintenance and Emergency Services, and Traffic Electrical Planned Capital Works Roster
topics: agreements, contracts, electric distribution utilities, electricity, traffic
brief: Approving no-bid 1-year deals for traffic signal maintenance: Black & McDonald at $17,745,351 ($18,057,669) and TM3 at $5,851,671 ($5,954,660), plus roster figures of $19,894,553 ($20,244,697), $500,000, $16,027,600 ($16,309,686), and $4,552,388 ($4,632,510). It goes to City Council for approval.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $17,745,351.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with ServiceNow Canada Inc., for Licenses and Professional Services
brief: Approving a no-bid 3-year $13,508,403 ($13,746,151 net of HST recoveries) deal directly with ServiceNow for the city's IT service platform. It goes to City Council for approval. A $500,000 figure is also cited.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $13,508,403.

title: Non-Competitive Procurement Contract with SmartSimple Software Inc., for New Configuration of the Toronto Grants, Rebates and Incentives Portal for Housing Secretariat
topics: affordable housing, contracts, purchasing, software, subsidies and grants
brief: Approving a no-bid 2-year $300,000 ($305,280 net of HST recoveries) SmartSimple deal to rebuild the housing grants portal. It goes to City Council for approval. Also cited: $27 million, $100 million, and $500,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $300,000.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order 6049718 with Veolia Water Canada Inc., for Critical Capital Improvements and Maintenance at the Disco Organics Processing Facility
topics: agreements, contracts, organics processing facilities, water
brief: The city wants to amend its Veolia deal to fund urgent repairs at the Disco Road organics plant ahead of a planned expansion. No dollar figures are given.

title: Simplifying the 311 Intake Experience
topics: non emergency municipal services, public inquiries
brief: A committee wants staff to report back with a plan to make 311 calls simpler and clearer about how service requests are ranked.

title: Review of Parking and Transit Related Requests for Etobicoke York District
brief: A councillor asks city planners to study whether pausing the removal of minimum parking rules for new buildings in Etobicoke York is possible until transit improves.

title: Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal 2025 Annual Report
brief: This is for information only: the committee receives the Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal's 2025 annual report on its operations. No policy change is proposed.

title: 34 Jason Road - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: City Council plans to designate the Elm Bank Piggery property at 34 Jason Road in Etobicoke's Thistletown community as a heritage property.

title: 328 Bellamy Road North - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: City Council plans to designate the J.P. Wheler House at 328 Bellamy Road North in Scarborough as a heritage property.

title: 339 Queen Street East - Proposed Amendment to Designating By-law under Part IV, Section 30.1 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: City Council will decide whether to update the heritage designation for 339 Queen Street East with details about its furniture store history, Chicago School style, and timber frame construction.

title: Metrolinx Eglinton Crosstown LRT - At-grade Segment and Tunnel Section - Traffic and Parking By-law Amendments and Road Dedication
topics: light rail transit, municipal codes, parking regulations
brief: Approving the last traffic and parking by-law changes for the Eglinton Crosstown LRT corridor (Kennedy to Weston) and dedicate new road lands as public highway. It goes to Council for approval.

title: Right-Turn-on-Red Prohibition - Victoria Park Avenue and Kingston Road
brief: Banning southbound right turns on red at Victoria Park and Kingston Road, where TTC streetcar tracks clash with turning cars. It goes to Council for a decision.

title: Concerns and Considerations raised by the Province of Ontario and Energy Utilities regarding Development in Proximity to the Hearn Switching Station
topics: controller cabinets (traffic), official plan amendments, utilities
brief: This is an information item: staff present the province's and utilities' concerns about development near the Hearn Switching Station, tied to an appeal for 402 and 440 Unwin Avenue.
stake: About controller cabinets (traffic). Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: 4150 Yonge Street - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: City Council plans to designate the John Street Workers Cottages at 4150 Yonge Street in North York as a heritage property.

title: Establishing the Lawrence Heights Neighbourhood Centre in the Association of Community Centres
brief: A decision on setting up the Lawrence Heights Neighbourhood Centre as a new community-centre board of management, with 12 members including 11 public members and the Ward 8 councillor sits with Council.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Heritage Toronto Board of Directors
brief: Appointing eight public members, including one Indigenous community member, to the Heritage Toronto Board for terms ending June 26, 2030. It goes to City Council for approval. The nominees' details stay private.

title: Update on MM40.20 - Reinstating Paddle the Don for 2027
brief: This is an information item: the committee gets a report on possibly reviving the Paddle the Don canoe event in 2027, which ran from 1993 to 2019.
stake: About conservation. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 22 in favour, none against.

title: Establishing Toronto's Cultural Districts Program
brief: Council will weigh whether to have staff set up a Cultural Districts Program in phases, starting with formal recognition of culturally distinct areas such as Little Jamaica and Church-Wellesley Village, to celebrate them and help respond to the loss of cultural identity from displacement.

title: Renaming Tichester Park in Honour of Hedy Bohm
brief: Renaming Tichester Park to Hedy Bohm Park, honouring a Holocaust survivor and longtime local resident known for Holocaust education and community work heads to City Council for a decision.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Lakeshore Arena Corporation Board
brief: Appointing two public members and one tenant representative to the Lakeshore Arena Corporation Board for terms ending June 26, 2028. It goes to City Council for approval. The nominees' details stay private.

title: Updates on Vision Zero Road Safety Initiatives: Enhancing Safety in School Zones, Permanent Roadside Memorials, Changes to Parking Regulations for Intersection Pedestrian Signals, and Road Safety Improvement Projects
topics: memorials, parking, parking regulations, pedestrian signals, road safety, safety, schools, traffic control systems
brief: The committee receives a Vision Zero update on school-zone safety (more police enforcement after speed cameras ended), a permanent roadside memorial program, parking changes near pedestrian signals, and new safety projects. The recommended projects would cost $6,193,000 to install, already funded in the capital budget.
stake: About memorials. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 23 in favour, none against.

title: Western Beaches Public Realm Plan
topics: beaches, parks and open space areas, public realm, waterfronts
brief: This is an information item: the committee receives the Western Beaches public realm plan for the waterfront between the Humber River and Ontario Place.

title: Preserving Affordable Homes at 38 Abell Street and 210 Simcoe Streets
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve long-term nominal leases with a new operator to preserve affordable homes at 38 Abell Street and 210 Simcoe Street after the Artscape non-profit became insolvent.

title: Authority to Enter into Municipal Housing Project Facility Agreements with Community Housing Providers
brief: City Council will decide whether to grant property tax exemptions for affordable homes at three co-op sites and two Toronto Community Housing properties to help keep rents affordable.

title: Humber Bay Shores, Christie's Redevelopment and Park Lawn GO Station
brief: This is a routine item: City Council will receive a report on tools to support Humber Bay Shores as a complete community with higher-order transit, including planned facilities tied to the Christie's redevelopment and Park Lawn GO Station.
stake: About public transit. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 24 in favour, none against.

title: Call to Order
brief: City Council opens its meeting with O Canada and a moment of silence.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: City Council confirms the minutes from its May 20 and 21, 2026 meeting.

title: Toronto Local Appeal Body - Chair's 2025 Annual Report
brief: This is a routine item: the Planning and Housing Committee will receive the Toronto Local Appeal Body Chair's 2025 annual report. The tribunal hears appeals of Committee of Adjustment decisions.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports, New Business and Business Previously Requested from City Officials
brief: City Council formally introduces the committee reports it will consider at this meeting.

brief: Council members declare any conflicts of interest under provincial law.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Petitions
brief: Council members may file petitions.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: Various presentations and announcements are made at the council meeting.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: City Council reviews the Order Paper listing its business.

title: Amendment to Municipal Code Chapter 27 (Council Procedures) and Municipal Code Chapter 925 (Permit Parking): Streamlining Permit Parking Exclusions for New Developments
brief: City Council will decide whether to exclude new developments from on-street permit parking eligibility and keep those decisions with full council.

title: Improving Access to Toronto Island Park - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: This motion asks council to have staff study cheaper ways to visit Toronto Island, including discounted ferry fares and removing passenger fees, and to report back through the 2027 budget process.

title: City of Toronto Investment Report for the Year 2025
brief: This is a routine item: council is asked to receive the city's 2025 investment report, which shows returns of $391.0 million and approximately $85 million. Nothing changes.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $391.0 million.

brief: Council will weigh whether to approve a pedestrian crossing on Maple Leaf Drive and a Community Safety Zone on Falstaff Avenue, where traffic fines are doubled.

title: 390, 394, 396 and 398 Spadina Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Approving a 14-storey building at 390 to 398 Spadina Road with 54 homes and ground-floor shops heads to City Council for a decision. The owner must help the five existing rental tenants affected by demolition.

brief: A builder proposed a 29-storey, 423-home building at 2915-2943 Bloor Street West, then appealed. Staff want city lawyers to oppose the current version and keep negotiating.

brief: City Council has the final say on whether to extend construction closures around River Street and Labatt Avenue to December 2029 for a 34-storey rental building that had been paused. The affected parking machines charge $3.25 per hour.

brief: City Council will review Metrolinx's plan to rebuild the Birchmount Road bridge over the GO Lakeshore East rail line.

brief: Approving a 7-storey building with 40 homes and a small shop at 179-181 Finch Avenue East. It goes to City Council for approval.

brief: This is routine business. City Council receives the 2024 audited financial statements and management letter for Moss Park Arena, for information. No decision is needed.

brief: The Auditor General asks Council to have the City's real estate division improve its rules for extra costs on large building projects, covering who approves them, spending limits and paperwork.

title: Riverside District Business Improvement Area Expansion Poll Results

brief: Council is set to decide whether to expand the Riverside District BIA boundary, after a poll where most accepted ballots favoured expansion, and to have staff run further consultations with City divisions on the expansion.

title: 3000, 3004, 3008, 3012 and 3020 Kennedy Road - Draft Plan of Subdivision Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council is being advised that staff plan to approve the subdivision at 3000-3020 Kennedy Road under delegated authority.

brief: City Council will decide whether to approve a 24-storey building with 419 homes at 3718-3730 Kingston Road.

title: 3140, 3150 and 3170 Dufferin Street and 60 and 68 Apex Road - Class 4 Noise Area Classification (NPC-300) - Final Report
brief: Naming the lands at 3140–3170 Dufferin Street and 60 and 68 Apex Road a Class 4 noise area for a new mixed-use development with four residential towers. It goes to City Council for a decision.

brief: Naming the lands at 3180 Dufferin Street a Class 4 noise area for a new mixed-use development with four residential towers. It goes to City Council for a decision.

title: The Peanut Streets Plan - Protected Pedestrian Crossings
brief: Approving protected pedestrian crossings at two spots on Don Mills Road and one on Van Horne Avenue as part of The Peanut Streets Plan. It goes to City Council for approval.

brief: Changing zoning so Metrolinx can build Yonge North Subway Extension and Ontario Line facilities like substations and station entrances. It goes to City Council for a decision.

title: 8 Parmbelle Crescent - Zoning Amendment Application - Final Report - Refusal
topics: land use, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws
brief: Refusing four three-storey townhouses at 8 Parmbelle Crescent, which staff say do not fit the area's character. It goes to City Council for a decision.

brief: Up for a decision before Council: add a two-space electric vehicle charging area on Lake Shore Boulevard West, and remove rules for a charger at 2000 Weston Road that was taken out.

title: 954, 956 and 958 Broadview Avenue and 72 Chester Hill Road - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: official plan amendments, rezoning, zoning, zoning bylaws
brief: The decision on whether to approve growing a 14-storey project at 954-958 Broadview Avenue to 26 storeys, with 309 homes including eight affordable units, keeping heritage repairs and a public park rests with City Council. stake: About official plan amendments. Decided by a recorded vote, 20 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

title: Metrolinx Scarborough Subway Extension - Temporary Traffic Modifications and Public Highway Dedications - Kennedy Station Connection, Emergency Exit Building-3, and Scarborough Centre Station
brief: City Council will decide whether to adjust temporary road closures for the next phase of Scarborough Subway Extension construction.

title: 614 Danforth Road - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Refusal
brief: City Council will decide whether to refuse a 33-storey building with 380 homes at 614 Danforth Road.

topics: Exhibition Place, activities in science and technology, audits, security
brief: Approving releasing the Auditor General's second cybersecurity audit report on Exhibition Place, covering network security and key systems. It goes to City Council for approval. The venue generates $595 million a year in economic impact and earned $67.3 million in revenue in 2024.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $595 million.

title: Investigation into the Procurement of the PayIt Platform
brief: This is routine business. City Council receives the Auditor General's investigation into how the City bought the PayIt platform, for information. No decision is needed.

stake: The official summary names a figure of $7.250 million.

brief: Authorizing a new Heritage Organization Operating Partnership program giving operating funding to not-for-profit heritage organizations, completing a multi-year reform of the City's culture grants is on Council's agenda.

brief: This is for information only: council receives an update on the February 6, 2026 Ontario's Big City Mayors meeting, covering the 2026 provincial pre-budget ask, health care pressures and municipal tax reform. The report notes over $1.5 billion in property tax funding goes to housing and social services.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1.5 billion.

title: Report on Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) Committee Meetings - February 2026

brief: City Council plans to designate the property at 65 Heward Avenue, including 87 Heward Avenue, as a heritage property.

brief: Adopting updates to its 10-year economic action plan, including actions from the mayor's US-tariff response plan and new actions on inclusive economic development is on Council's agenda.

brief: Up for a decision before Council: let staff set rules for paying back insurance costs for non-profits, charities and community groups that run outdoor ovens in parks for public events. The report cites $10,000.

stake: The official summary names a figure of $11 billion.

brief: City Council will decide whether to oppose converting 65-87 Heward Avenue from employment land to mixed-use at the Ontario Land Tribunal. City staff recommend fighting it.

stake: The official summary names a figure of $207,000.00.

brief: City Council will decide whether to keep 1767 and 1773 Bayview Avenue and 73 Niagara Street on the City's Heritage Register despite the owners' objections.

brief: An eastbound bus queue-jump lane on Lawrence Avenue West — plus road and parking changes, which a study team found would ease congestion without harming future plans — is up for community council approval.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with RideShark Corporation for the Smart Commute Online Tool

brief: Approving five no-bid deals totalling $7,085,485, ($7,210,190 net of HST recoveries) for proprietary water plant parts: $2,654,568 ($2,701,288), $1,592,741 ($1,620,773), $1,150,000 ($1,170,240), $1,141,464 ($1,161,554), and $546,713 ($556,335). stake: The official summary names a figure of $7,085,485.

brief: Adding $11,159,260 ($11,355,663 net of HST recoveries) to the Amazon cloud contract and extend it a year, raising it from $447,059 ($454,927) to $11,606,318 ($11,810,589). It goes to City Council for a decision.

waste water treatment plants, sewage treatment
brief: A member motion raises recent odour from the Ashbridges Bay treatment plant after a holding-tank breakdown, questioning why the local councillor wasn't told of the failure and asking for better odour-complaint communication.

topics: Toronto Transit Commission, expropriations, projects, subways, transit networks
brief: Starting expropriating temporary easements at 2 and 90 Bloor Street East to expand Bloor-Yonge station. It goes to City Council for a decision. Owners get 30 days to ask for a hearing.

brief: Approving an $800,000 ($814,080 net of HST recoveries) no-bid bridge contract with Safeguard Perimeter for traffic control gear at major events from June to December 2026; a $500,000 figure is also cited. It goes to City Council for approval.

topics: contracts, software, traffic, transportation, transportation projects
brief: Approving no-bid software deals: Aimsun at $115,000 USD ($117,024 USD) and PTV Group at $219,861 USD ($223,731 USD) for traffic modelling tools, each 5 years. It goes to City Council for approval. A $500,000 figure is also cited.

brief: This is for information only: council receives a report on development options for a mixed-income affordable housing project on City-owned land at 838 Broadview Avenue. Money details stay private for property talks. No policy change is proposed.

title: Amendments to the TTC Records Retention Schedule (Municipal Code Chapter 219, Records, Corporate (Local Boards))

title: Establishing an Accessible Loading Zone on Oakwood Avenue
topics: accessibility, loading zones, parking, parking regulations
brief: It's City Council's call whether to create an accessible loading zone on Oakwood Avenue, open 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. daily, so a resident can safely use TTC Wheel-Trans. Two daytime parking spots would be removed.

title: Ontario Place Event - RBC Amphitheatre 2026 Traffic Management Strategy
brief: The decision on letting Live Nation put up temporary fencing on Lake Shore Boulevard West from May to October 2026, as part of its traffic plan for concerts at the Ontario Place venue rests with City Council.

title: Review of Parking and Transit Related Requests for Scarborough
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie is asking City Council to study pausing the removal of minimum parking rules for new Scarborough developments until transit improves, and to look at blocking new developments from on-street parking permits.
stake: About parking. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

title: Supporting the Proposed Modernization of Ontario’s Framework for Power-Assisted Bicycles (E-Bikes)
brief: Councillor Saxe asks Council to back Ontario's proposed e-bike rules: pedal e-bikes capped at 32 km/h and 500 watts, while faster moped-style vehicles would need licences and insurance.
stake: About by-laws. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 26 in favour, none against.

title: Call to Order
brief: City Council opens its meeting with O Canada and a moment of silence.
stake: A citywide decision. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: City Council confirms the minutes from its April 22 and 23, 2026 meeting.

title: Payment of Legal Expenses Related to an Integrity Commissioner Investigation
brief: Paying back Councillor Chris Moise $20,807.61 for legal costs from an Integrity Commissioner investigation, under the council members' operations policy is on Council's agenda.
stake: About refund. Decided by a recorded vote, 18 in favour and 4 against — every member's position is public.

title: Responding to Bill 98, Building Homes and Improving Transportation Infrastructure Act, 2026 - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: This motion asks council to endorse the TTC board's principles for staff joining provincial talks on a law that would give Ontario's transportation minister powers over regional transit fares and service rules.
stake: About public transit. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 21 in favour, none against.

title: Towards a Vision for a Design Standard for Future Toronto Subway Stations - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: This motion asks council to have the TTC, the City, and Metrolinx study a design standard for all new subway stations, including platform screen doors, public washrooms, bike parking, and tall well-lit ceilings above platforms.
stake: About public transit. Decided by a recorded vote, 15 in favour and 9 against — every member's position is public.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports, New Business and Business Previously Requested from the Mayor and City Officials
brief: City Council formally introduces the committee reports it will consider at this meeting.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: Council members declare any conflicts of interest under provincial law.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Petitions
brief: Council members may file petitions.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: Various presentations and announcements are made at the council meeting.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: City Council reviews the Order Paper listing its business.

title: It’s Time to Reinstate Cummer Station for the North York Centre - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: This motion asks council to seek federal and provincial funding to bring back the previously dropped Cummer Station on the Yonge North Subway Extension, to serve planned growth around North York Centre.
stake: About public transit. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 23 in favour, none against.

title: Exploring a Garden of Achievement with Canada’s Walk of Fame
topics: activities in community and life, locations in community and life
brief: This motion asks council to have City divisions work with Canada's Walk of Fame to develop a concept plan for improving the public space around David Pecaut Square, as part of a proposed Garden of Achievement honouring notable Canadians.
stake: About activities in community and life.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Common Table - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe asks council to release $150,000 ($150,000) in developer funds to replace the unreliable freight elevator serving the Common Table drop-in for homeless people in the Church of the Redeemer's basement.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $150,000.

title: Authorization to Reallocate Section 37 Funds from Royal Rouge Tot Lot Park Improvements to the Dogs Off-Leash Area at Lawrence Avenue East and Starspray Boulevard - by Councillor Neethan Shan, seconded by Councillor Paul Ainslie
brief: Councillor Neethan Shan asks council to move $200,000 in developer funds from the Royal Rouge Tot Lot project to a new dogs off-leash area at Lawrence Avenue East and Starspray Boulevard.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $200,000.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Board of Directors of TO Live
brief: Recommending three candidates to City Council for the TO Live Board for a term ending May 23, 2030. It goes to the Civic Appointments Committee for a decision. Candidate details stay private.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Toronto Pan Am Sports Centre Board
brief: Appointing two public members to the Toronto Pan Am Sports Centre Board for a term ending May 22, 2028. It goes to City Council for approval. The nominees' details stay private.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority Board
brief: Picking four candidates to interview for the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority Board, then recommend one to Council. It goes to the Civic Appointments Committee for approval. Candidate details stay private.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Administrative Penalty Tribunal
brief: Appointing Stephen Scharbach to the Administrative Penalty Tribunal, which reviews certain City penalties, for a term ending April 25, 2030. It goes to Council for approval. Other application details stay private.

title: 2912 to 2926 Sheppard Avenue East - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment Applications - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on a Tribunal hearing about a proposed 50-storey mixed-use building with 590 homes at 2912 to 2926 Sheppard Avenue East. Details stay private as legal advice.

title: 112 Walmer Road - Development Charges Complaint and Parkland Levy Appeal - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on an appeal over building fees and a parkland levy for a five-unit project with a garden suite at 112 Walmer Road. Details stay private as legal advice.
stake: About development charges. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on a Tribunal hearing about a zoning change request for 1149 and 1153 Queen Street West, which Council turned down. Details stay private as legal advice.

brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on a Tribunal hearing about three proposed mixed-use towers (39 to 49 storeys) at 2 to 4 and 80 Union Street. Details stay private as legal advice.

brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on the ongoing Tribunal appeal for 5051 to 5061 Yonge Street, where Council accepted a 2024 settlement for a 55-storey building with on-site community space, and the matter remains under appeal. Details stay private as legal advice.

title: Standardizing the Air Conditioner Benefit (Pilot)
topics: benefits, heating, ventilation and air conditioning systems, pilot projects
brief: The decision on adding $1,060,000 from the extreme weather reserve to give portable air conditioners to low-income residents as extreme heat protection, supplying up to 2,400 units in summer 2026 rests with Council. The report's figures also include $1,041,667, $1,092,200, $1,111,422, $2,133,867, and $2,171,423.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1,060,000. Decided by a recorded vote, 23 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie asks council to review all city cricket facilities and report back by early 2027 with a costed, prioritized action plan on seating, washrooms, fields and enforcement. No dollar figure is set yet.

brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie asks council to request Ontario let unhoused people on social assistance keep and save their shelter allowance toward first and last month's rent.
stake: About subsidies and grants. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 3 against — every member's position is public.

brief: Council gets an update on marker buoys showing where motorized boats cannot go in the Port of Toronto. It approved a $310,500 transfer to buy and install the buoys in 2026, with the money flowing to the Toronto Port Authority.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Toronto Licensing Tribunal
brief: Appointing Yizhe Chi and Deborah Moriah to the Toronto Licensing Tribunal, which handles licensing appeals, for a term ending November 14, 2026. It goes to Council for approval. Other application details stay private.

brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for permission to have a land-dispute board review its decision on a development at 151 and 161 to 181 Mulock Avenue and 6 Lloyd Avenue. Details stay private as legal advice.

brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on a Tribunal hearing about four proposed towers with 2,170 homes, including affordable ones, at 155 St. Dennis Drive. Details stay private as legal advice.

brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe asks council to have the City Manager review and standardize training for by-law enforcement officers and special constables across city divisions.

stake: Ward 15 is named in the record. Decided by a recorded vote, 23 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: 2351 and 2355 Keele Street - Zoning By- Law Amendment Application - Request for Directions Report
brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on a Tribunal hearing about a proposed 25-storey building with 311 homes at 2351 and 2355 Keele Street. Details stay private as legal advice.

stake: About courts. Decided by a recorded vote, 20 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: 8 Arnold Avenue - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
brief: Adding 8 Arnold Avenue to the City's heritage list for its cultural value. It goes to Council for a decision. It is an 1870s red-brick farmhouse-style home called the George Marshall Residence in Mount Dennis.

title: 180 Queens Drive - Notice of Intention to Designate a Property under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act
brief: Saying it plans to protect 180 Queens Drive as a heritage property for its cultural value. It goes to Council for a decision. An earlier plan expired because the paperwork was not finished within 120 days.

brief: Approving changes to two heritage-protected buildings — the former Wilton Court Hotel at 212 Dundas Street East and 275 George Street — as part of building a new 44-storey residential building on the site. It goes to Council for approval.

brief: Councillor Myers (Ward 23) filed an inquiry about SmartTrack accounting: the city has received no Metrolinx invoices since 2018 despite about $184 million in costs, per an Auditor General report. $186 million is also cited.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $184 million. Council sent it back for more work.

title: Request for Federal Proclamation of February as Chinese Canadian Heritage Month - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng asks council to request the federal government proclaim February as Chinese Canadian Heritage Month.

title: Strengthening Compliance and Coordination Across Multiplex Development-Related Enforcement Processes - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo asks council to strengthen enforcement coordination on multiplex construction sites after complaints about by-law violations, unpermitted work and tree damage.

title: Accepting an In-Kind Donation from Wanless Park Community Tennis Club to Refurbish the Tennis Courts at Wanless Park - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin asks council to accept an in-kind donation of up to $319,000 from the Wanless Park Community Tennis Club to rebuild two courts and resurface all five at 250 Wanless Avenue.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $319,000.

title: Strengthening the Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement to Support Economic Prosperity in Toronto and the Great Lakes Region - by Councillor Paul Ainslie, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: Councillor Paul Ainslie asks council to back the St. Catharines resolution urging Ottawa to preserve the Canada-U.S.-Mexico trade agreement at its 2026 review, noting about $2.7 trillion in annual trilateral trade.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $2.7.

brief: Councillor Parthi Kandavel asks council to assess whether Bluffer's Park West Beach could host seasonal off-leash dog hours, as an interim step while Scarborough awaits more off-leash areas.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
brief: This is routine business. General bills and confirming bills will come before City Council, the formal step that makes Council's decisions law.

title: Authorization to Extend a Nominal Fee Licence Agreement with the 519 Community Centre at Barbara Hall Park - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
brief: This is procedural: council is asked to extend The 519's nominal-fee licence to keep running programs and events in Barbara Hall Park after its August 2025 expiry.
stake: Ward 13 is named in the record.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds - Improving Mercer Street Streetscape - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik asks council to release $1,500,000 in developer funds for the Mercer Street streetscape rebuild: $375,000 in 2026 and $1,125,000 in 2027, covering new paving, bollards, bike rings and loading zones.

brief: Councillor Chris Moise asks council to release $4,700 ($4,700.00) in developer funds for rainbow branded street name signs marking the Church-Wellesley Village boundaries.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $4,700.

brief: Councillor Chris Moise asks council to release $50,000 ($50,000.00) in developer funds to the Church-Wellesley Village BIA for planters, disposal receptacles and pole wraps along Church Street for the pedestrianization pilot.

title: Implementation of New Municipal Requirements under the Buy Ontario Act, 2025
brief: Changing City buying rules, starting May 25, 2026, to choose Ontario-made goods first, then Canadian-made, as required by the province's new Buy Ontario law. It goes to Council for a decision.

title: Allocating Community Benefit Charges from 41 to 47 Hendon Avenue Development to Improve Hendon Park - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng asks council to earmark Community Benefits Charges from the 41-47 Hendon Avenue development for Hendon Park improvements through the 2027 budget. No dollar figure is in the source.
stake: Ward 18 is named in the record.

brief: Councillor Lily Cheng asks council to seek provincial legislation enabling noise camera enforcement against excessive vehicle noise in Toronto.
stake: About noise control. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

brief: Councillor Chris Moise asks council to release $100,000.00 in developer funds to the Friends of Allan Gardens for Greenhouse Link Building drawings. The source also lists a $10 million figure for the Allan Gardens expansion.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $10 million.

title: Making it Easier to Build More Housing: Extending Development Charge Incentives to Condominium Multiplexes and Engaging on the Review of the Ontario Building Code
brief: Extending home-building fee discounts to condo multiplexes and to work with the province on simpler building rules, to make new homes easier and cheaper to build. It goes to Council for approval.

brief: This is just for information: council receives the Ombudsman Toronto's 2025 annual report, as required by law. No decision is needed.

brief: This is just for information: council receives a follow-up report on the 2026 review of street-vending and street-artist rules, including how to cut loud noise near homes and Sankofa Square. No decision is needed.

brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik asks council to review the Toronto Island ferry fare structure, including discounted and fee-free ticketing options, ahead of two new ferries arriving in 2027.
stake: About accessibility. Decided by a recorded vote, 18 in favour and 7 against — every member's position is public.

brief: Councillor Parthi Kandavel asks council to review public parking access at Scarborough GO Station, where commuter cars spill onto residential streets, and look at underused nearby lands.

brief: Councillor Parthi Kandavel asks council to plan for Bluffer's Park's growth: better signage now, plus expanded parking and neighbourhood protections ahead of a new Brimley Road trail bringing more visitors.

brief: Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin asks council to add pedestrian and cyclist safety messaging to end-of-school-year campaigns, covering phone use while crossing, earbuds, and e-scooter and e-bike rules.

brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik asks council to speak out against Toronto District School Board cuts under provincial supervision and express support for keeping outdoor education, family engagement, behaviour support, library and equity programs.

brief: Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin asks council to press for accurate in-station arrival displays on Line 5, where screens have shown times unrelated to actual trains since opening.

brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher asks council to approve a one-time $151,100 stabilization grant for the Alumnae Theatre Company at 70 Berkeley Street.

brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher asks council to create a bi-annual Affordable Housing Awards of Excellence honouring the partners who build and manage new rental homes.
stake: About affordable housing. Decided by a recorded vote, 24 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo asks council to accept a $700,000 Health Canada grant for equity-focused training curriculum for the Toronto Community Crisis Service.

title: 45 Grenoble Drive - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: by-laws, development, multi-residential properties, property (sc), zoning
brief: Approving a 40-storey building with 405 homes at 45 Grenoble Drive, while keeping the existing 217 rental homes on the site. It goes to City Council for approval.

title: Highway 27 and Rexdale Boulevard - Pedestrian Crossing Protection
brief: Adding three pedestrian crossings and two yield signs at Highway 27 and Rexdale Boulevard, and fix a mismatch between signs and current rules is on Council's agenda.

title: 3459 and 3461 Dundas Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Whether to approve a seven-storey building at 3459 and 3461 Dundas Street West with 45 homes and ground-floor shops now sits with City Council.

title: 1423 Dufferin Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: City Council is set to decide whether to approve a nine-storey building at 1423 Dufferin Street with 60 rental homes and shops below. The building would not get overnight street parking permits.

title: Lake Shore Boulevard East - Mid-Block Pedestrian and Cyclist Traffic Control Signal and Public Realm Improvements
topics: cyclists, pedestrians, public realm, traffic control systems
pedestrianization, public spaces, traffic signal control systems
brief: The community council has the final say on whether to install a mid-block traffic light for pedestrians and cyclists on Lake Shore Boulevard East near Cherry Street, closing a gap in the waterfront trail. Northbound left turns there would be banned.
stake: About cyclists. Council sent it back for more work.

title: 8 Prince Arthur Avenue - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property Under Section 42 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Approval
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties
brief: The decision on whether to approve adding three storeys to the rear of the heritage building at 8 Prince Arthur Avenue for expanded offices, with a plan to protect its historic features rests with City Council.

title: 171 East Liberty Street - Inclusion on the Heritage Register
topics: heritage designation, heritage preservation, heritage properties
brief: Whether to add 171 East Liberty Street, a 1942 factory complex built for the John Inglis Company, to the Heritage Register now sits with City Council. Listing is a first step toward possible protection.

title: 1196-1210 Yonge Street and 2-8 Birch Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: demolitions, rental housing, residential tenants, tenants
brief: A decision on tearing down eight rentals at 1196-1210 Yonge Street and 2-8 Birch Avenue goes to City Council. The eight replacement rentals would be built off-site at Poplar Plains Road with tenant help, and the approval carries a $20,000.00 financial condition.

title: 93 York Road - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
topics: Official Plans, land use, zoning, zoning bylaws
brief: Approving six three-storey townhouses at 93 York Road. It goes to City Council for approval.

title: Accessible Parking Spaces - April 2026 (Non-Delegated)
brief: City Council has the final say on whether to add new on-street accessible parking spaces for people with disabilities on streets with TTC service. This is a routine update.

title: 333 Lake Shore Boulevard East, 200 Queens Quay East, and 2, 11, and 11 R Small Street (Quayside Blocks 3, 4 and 5) - Draft Plan of Subdivision Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: This is a routine item: council is told staff plan to approve the draft subdivision plan for Quayside Blocks 3, 4, and 5, with two building sites, two parks, and two public streets. Final approval still has conditions.

title: 10 Rosehill Avenue - City-Initiated Temporary Use Zoning By-law - Decision Report - Approval
brief: The decision on approving a three-year trial letting the building at 10 Rosehill Avenue be used as a concert hall, event space, assembly hall, or broadcast studio rests with City Council.

title: 3286, 3290, 3296, 3298, 3300, 3308 and 3316 Dundas Street West - Zoning By-law Amendment - Decision Report - Approval
brief: Before City Council for a decision: approve an 11-storey mixed-use rental building at 3286 to 3316 Dundas Street West with 191 homes, including six replacement rentals, plus ground-floor shops and parking.

title: Exclusion of Bloor-Dufferin from On-Street Residential Permit Parking
topics: accessible permit parking, parking, permit parking
brief: Council will weigh whether to have staff study whether the Bloor-Dufferin building project should be excluded from street permit parking. Excluding new buildings helps manage parking and supports walking, cycling, and transit.

title: Bayview Avenue - Parking Amendments
topics: parking, parking regulations, stopping prohibitions, traffic regulations
brief: City Council will weigh whether to relax a no-stopping rule to no-standing in a Bayview Avenue turn lane near Front Street East, so drivers and TTC buses can pick up and drop off riders.

title: 353 and 355 Adelaide Street West, 46 Charlotte Street and 16 Oxley Street - Community Benefits Charge In-kind Contribution
brief: The call on whether to let the developer of a 58-storey tower on Adelaide Street West provide ten affordable rental units for 25 years as its community benefit contribution, instead of paying part of the fee belongs to City Council.

title: Kennedy Road, at a point 140 metres north of Dancy Avenue -Traffic Control Signals
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, traffic control systems
brief: City Council will decide whether to install traffic signals on Kennedy Road north of Dancy Avenue.

title: Quayside Infrastructure and Public Realm Project (Phase 2) - Construction Staging Area
brief: Approving temporary closures near the waterfront — including part of the Martin Goodman Trail and sections of Queens Quay East — from April to December 2026 for Waterfront Toronto's Quayside infrastructure project goes to City Council for a decision.

title: 55 Lake Shore Boulevard East - Alterations to a Designated Heritage Property and Authority to Amend a Heritage Easement Agreement
topics: agreements, easements, heritage designation, heritage properties
brief: It's City Council's call whether to approve changes to the heritage former LCBO complex at 55 Lake Shore Boulevard East, with new buildings above the warehouse only, and to update the heritage easement agreement.

title: 55-77 Davisville Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval
brief: The decision on approving a 37-storey residential building at 55-77 Davisville Avenue, plus a new walkway and a small park rests with City Council. The existing 29-storey rental building with 483 units would stay.

title: 333 College Street and 303 Augusta Avenue - Community Benefits Charge In-kind Offer
brief: City Council decides whether to accept the developer's offer at 333 College Street and 303 Augusta Avenue: paving Ellen Avenue to city standards and researching title so nearby lanes can come into city ownership, as its community benefit contribution.

title: Bay Street and Edward Street - Traffic Control Signals
topics: traffic operations, traffic signal control systems
brief: City Council is set to decide whether to install traffic lights at Bay Street and Edward Street, which staff say will make the intersection safer. Stopping and parking rules on Edward Street would also change.

title: Pharmacy Avenue and Stellarton Road/Camilla Crescent - Traffic Control Signals
topics: traffic calming, traffic control systems, traffic signals
brief: City Council will decide whether to install traffic signals at Pharmacy Avenue and Stellarton Road/Camilla Crescent.

title: Nightstar Road - Traffic Calming (Speed Cushions) and Heavy Vehicle Prohibition
brief: City Council will decide on speed cushions and a heavy vehicle ban on Nightstar Road; staff recommend against the cushions.
stake: About assessment. Decided by a recorded vote, 23 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: 53-55 Yonge Street - Construction Staging Area Time Extension
topics: construction, parking prohibitions, road closures, road restrictions, stopping prohibitions
tripinfo, no parking, no stopping, street closures
brief: The call on whether to extend lane and sidewalk closures on Yonge Street and Colborne Street from May to July 2026 while two buildings are demolished ahead of future development belongs to City Council. The $6.75-per-hour parking rules would also change.

title: Traffic and Parking Amendments -  Toronto Transit Commission (TTC) Traction Power Upgrade Project
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, parking regulations, traffic regulations
brief: The decision on whether to temporarily remove paid parking — charged at $6.75 per hour — on parts of Granby and McGill streets from April to August 2026, to make room for TTC electrical work that supports more subway service rests with City Council.

title: Chinatown Tomorrow Planning Initiative - Proposals Report
brief: City Council has the final say on whether to approve using a draft West Chinatown growth plan for public consultation, with final recommendations due in July 2026. The plan aims to guide growth while keeping the area's character and heritage.
stake: About culture (sc). Its recorded vote was unanimous — 24 in favour, none against.

title: 49 Ontario Street (Phase 1) - Construction Staging Area
topics: construction, parking regulations, sidewalks, traffic regulations
brief: The call on whether to approve temporary sidewalk, cycle track, and lane closures around Adelaide Street East and Ontario Street from April 2026 to September 2027 for the first phase of two rental towers with affordable homes belongs to City Council. The $4.25-per-hour parking rules would also change.

title: 2351 and 2355 Keele Street - Zoning By-law Amendment Application- Appeal Report
brief: A builder proposed a 25-storey, 311-home building at 2351 and 2355 Keele Street, then appealed. Staff want city lawyers to oppose the current version and keep negotiating.

title: 130 Merton Street - Designation of a Portion of the Property used by Senior Peoples' Resources in North Toronto as a Municipal Capital Facility
topics: community centres, municipal facilities, properties (real estate), seniors, taxes
brief: Making part of 130 Merton Street (Unit 600, used by a seniors' non-profit) tax-exempt as a municipal capital facility. It goes to City Council for a decision.

title: Durham Boundary Facilities Agreement Renewal - Kingston Road Bridge over the Rouge River
brief: This is a procedural item: Council is asked to renew the cost-sharing deal with Durham Region for the Kingston Road Bridge over the Rouge River, with winter maintenance to Altona Road.

title: Traffic Control Signals - Victoria Park Avenue
topics: capital budgets, pedestrians, traffic control systems
brief: Approving traffic signals on Victoria Park Avenue at Belmore, Sloane, and Ruscica/Innismore, with some nearby pedestrian crossing bans. It goes to Council for approval.

title: Delegation of Authority for Crossing Agreements
brief: This is a procedural item: Council is asked to let the Parks and Recreation chief sign land-crossing agreements for approved capital projects without separate council votes.

title: Seeking Clarity on the City of Toronto's Application to the Community Sport and Recreation Infrastructure Fund
topics: administration, city-operated sports facilities, community centres, council items, funding, infrastructure, public inquiries, recreation centres, sports facilities
brief: This is a procedural item: a council inquiry about the city's application to the provincial sport and recreation fund goes to the committee for consideration.

title: Redesign Study of the Intersection of Eglinton Avenue West and the Allen Road Expressway - April 2026 Update
brief: This is an information item: the committee gets a progress report on the study to fix the congested Eglinton Avenue West and Allen Road intersection.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Upland Software Inc., for Telecom Expense Management Service
topics: contracts, information & communication (sc), purchasing, science & technology (sc), software
brief: Approving a no-bid $2,625,000 ($2,671,200 net of HST recoveries) deal with Upland Software for the Cimpl telecom expense tool, 3 years plus 2 renewals. It goes to City Council for approval. A $500,000 figure is also cited.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $2,625,000.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Microsoft Canada Inc., for M365 Software Licenses, Cloud Subscriptions, and Support Services
topics: contracts, information and communication technology, purchasing, software licences
brief: Approving a no-bid 5-year Microsoft 365 deal directly with Microsoft Canada for about 32,000 staff, since the current deal ends May 31, 2026. It goes to City Council for approval. A $500,000 figure is cited.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500,000.

title: Amendment to Non-Competitive Blanket Contract 4300000085 with City Dispensers Inc., for the Non-Exclusive Supply and Delivery of Prescription Eyewear for Toronto Employment and Social Services
topics: contracts, employment & labour (sc), health (sc), optometry services, purchasing
brief: Adding $1,500,000 to the eyeglasses contract for social assistance recipients, raising it from $500,000 to $2,000,000 and extending it to February 28, 2027. It goes to City Council for a decision.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1,500,000.

title: Non-Competitive Extension with Moneris Solutions Corporation for Payment Processing Services
brief: Giving Moneris a no-bid 3-year extension (2027-2029) for card payment processing while a new tender is on hold. It goes to City Council for a decision. Figures cited: $500,000 and $2,000,000, ($2,035,200, net of HST recoveries).
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500,000.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Wajax Limited for Repairs, Maintenance, Service Calls and Authorized Warranty Work on Allison Automatic Transmissions for Toronto Fire Services
topics: contracts, external services, fire and rescue services, fire trucks, purchasing
brief: Approving a no-bid deal with Wajax Limited for Allison transmission repairs on about 190 fire trucks, capped at $1,167,038 ($1,187,578 net of HST recoveries); $500,000 is also cited. It goes to City Council for approval.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1,167,038.

title: Congestion Management Plan - 2026 Spring Update
topics: congestion, traffic, traffic data, transportation research
brief: The committee receives the spring congestion update with the Chief Congestion Officer's first observations; $299.4 million is cited.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $299.4 million. Decided by a recorded vote, 15 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: The Electrification Advantage
brief: This is an information item: the committee receives the Electrification Advantage report on boosting local renewable energy and cutting natural gas use at the Portlands Energy Centre.

title: Non-Competitive Procurement Contract with Motorola Solutions Canada Inc., for the Provision of Enhanced Radio Communications Equipment at the St. Lawrence Market North Building
topics: city-owned properties, emergency services, purchasing, telecommunications
brief: Approving a $887,354 ($902,971 net of HST recoveries) no-bid Motorola deal to fix emergency radio dead zones in St. Lawrence Market North goes to City Council for approval; $500,000 is also cited.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500,000.

title: 2026 Property Tax Clawback Rate Report
topics: commercial areas, industrial properties, property tax rates, property taxes, residential properties, taxes
retail areas, industrial real estate, levies, municipal taxes
brief: Council decides whether to adopt the 2026 property tax clawback rates for commercial, industrial and multi-residential properties, needed to issue final tax bills and recover revenue lost from capping tax increases at 10 percent for properties with increases over $500.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500.

title: Business Improvement Areas (BIAs) - 2026 Operating Budgets - Report 2
topics: business improvement associations, budgets and accounts
brief: The decision on whether to approve 2026 operating budgets and special levies for 21 more Business Improvement Areas, funded by a special tax on commercial and industrial properties in each area rests with Council. The report's figures include $187,298.

title: Non-Competitive Agreements Required to Support the Existing and New Electric Ferries
stake: The official summary names a figure of $4,060,288.

title: Purchase Order Amendments for Professional Services and Non-Competitive Contract with Jordan Sook Studios Inc., for the Provision of Public Art - New Etobicoke Civic Centre
topics: civic centres, contracts, projects, public art, purchasing
brief: For the new Etobicoke Civic Centre, the city wants to amend project management contracts and award a no-bid public art deal to Jordan Sook Studios. Figures cited: $1,705,928 ($1,735,952), $20,234,075 ($20,590,194), $21,940,002 ($22,326,146), $2,310,827 ($2,351,498), $5,018,707 ($5,107,036), $7,329,534 ($7,458,533), $500,000, $514,250, and $523,301.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1,705,928.

title: City of Toronto Inclusive Economic Development Framework
brief: It's Council's call whether to adopt the Inclusive Economic Development Framework, aimed at ensuring residents and workers across the city can take part in and benefit from economic growth, as part of the City's 10-year economic plan.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Bramic Creative Business Products Ltd., for the Provision and Installation of Specialized Dispatch Consoles and Related Maintenance Services for Paramedic Services
brief: The city wants a $3,723,977 ($3,789,519 net of HST recoveries) no-bid deal with Bramic for paramedic dispatch consoles, 1 year plus 4 renewals; $500,000 is also cited.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $3,723,977.

title: Update on the Business Licence and Permit Applications Action Plan and Other Outstanding Directives
brief: This report updates the City's four-year plan to modernize business licensing. Council is asked to amend the licensing by-law, including removing fixed operating-hours rules and the handwritten ink-book requirement for certain goods registers.

title: Review of Toronto’s Street Vending and Artists By-laws
brief: Before Council for a decision: make interim changes to street vending rules, including new sidewalk food-vending permits in Wards 10, 11 and 13 and removing the five-hour vending limit. The report's dollar figures are $1,000,000,, $4,465.84, $2,429.07, $5,000.00, $2,500.00, $3,750.00, $512.66, $387.50, $258.33, $25.63, $250.00, $140.00, $65.00, $47.58, $25.08, $100.00, $200.00, $474.52, $351.16, $758.01, $370.08, $1,407.83, and $955.92.
stake: About by-laws. Decided by a recorded vote, 3 in favour and 19 against — every member's position is public.

title: 2700 Dufferin Street - Official Plan Amendment Application - Appeal Report
brief: City Council will decide whether to oppose converting most of 2700 Dufferin Street from employment land to mixed-use at the Ontario Land Tribunal. City staff recommend fighting it.

title: 110 West Toronto Street - Official Plan Amendment Application - Appeal Report
brief: City Council will decide whether to oppose converting 110 West Toronto Street from employment land to mixed-use at the Ontario Land Tribunal. City staff recommend fighting it.

title: 105-109 Vanderhoof Avenue and 10 Brentcliffe Road - Official Plan Amendment Application - Appeal Report
brief: City Council will decide whether to oppose converting 105-109 Vanderhoof Avenue and 10 Brentcliffe Road from employment land to mixed-use at the Ontario Land Tribunal. City staff recommend fighting it.
stake: About appeals. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 23 in favour, none against.

title: RentSafeTO Update
brief: City Council will decide whether to set a $42.73 or $46.81 fee to replace a building's RentSafeTO rating sign, waived for social housing, starting June 15, 2026. The item also lists penalty amounts of $500, $100.00, $501, $1,000, $200.00, $1,001, $2,000, $400.00, $2,001, $5,000, $1,000.00, $5,001, $10,000, and $2,000.00.
stake: About enforcement. Decided by a recorded vote, 23 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Status Update Report on Transit Oriented Communities
brief: City Council will decide whether to approve agreements with the province for the Transit Oriented Communities program, which pairs housing and development with GO stations like Guildwood GO.

title: 108-162 Vine Avenue - Official Plan Amendment Application - Appeal Report
brief: City Council will decide whether to oppose converting 108-162 Vine Avenue from employment land to mixed-use and parks at the Ontario Land Tribunal. City staff recommend fighting it.

title: Irene So - Appeal DDRT2026-04
brief: The Dangerous Dog Review Tribunal will hear appeal DDRT2026-04 against a dangerous dog order issued February 27, 2026. It decides one case, not policy.

title: 601, 625, and 673 Lake Shore Boulevard East, 185 Villiers Street, and 300 Commissioners Street - City-initiated "Meanwhile Use" enabling Policy and Zoning, and Update on McCleary District Planning Work
brief: City Council will decide whether to allow temporary 'meanwhile uses' like film, arts, sports, and retail on vacant or underused land in the McCleary District along Lake Shore Boulevard East.

title: Morrish Road - Traffic Calming
brief: City Council will decide whether to install speed cushions on Morrish Road.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto Mobility Plan: Temporary Adjustments to Traffic and Parking Regulations
brief: The decision on authorizing temporary traffic and parking by-law changes, parking exemptions and road closures as needed during the FIFA World Cup 2026 tournament to manage travel demand and support transit and emergency access rests with Council.

title: Towards a Beautiful City: Update on Priority Items
brief: This is for information only: council receives an update on eight priority items for improving the public realm, such as streets, parks, plazas and the waterfront. No policy change is proposed.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Toronto: By-law Exemptions to Facilitate Planning and Delivery of the FIFA World Cup 2026 Events at Fort York and the Bentway, and at Nathan Phillips Square
topics: festivals and special events, fireworks, special occasion permits, sports tournaments
brief: Council has the final say on whether to authorize exemptions to certain by-laws to deliver FIFA World Cup 2026 events at Fort York, the Bentway and Nathan Phillips Square, including an exemption allowing the sale of plastic bottled water alongside City water trailers.

title: Critical Investments in Streetlight Infrastructure for Public Safety
topics: infrastructure, investment, public safety & protection (sc), street lights
brief: Before Council for a decision: authorize talks to update the 2006 streetlighting service agreement with Toronto Hydro and approve a multi-year investment framework cited at $577 million, since much of the system, which includes 173,100 lights and 56,900 poles, has reached or exceeded its useful life.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $577 million. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 23 in favour, none against.

title: Toronto Personal Watercraft Safety Plan
brief: The decision on whether to adopt a Personal Watercraft Safety Plan for unsafe jet ski use along the waterfront, and to thank the Toronto Port Authority for motorized watercraft exclusion zones at three beaches in 2026 and request their continuation rests with Council.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Toronto Hydro Board
brief: This is a procedural item: the Corporations Nominating Panel will interview six candidates and suggest three, including a chair, for the Toronto Hydro Board.
stake: About public appointments. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 22 in favour, none against.

title: Implementation of a Commercial Loading Zone on Queen Street East
brief: City Council has the final say on whether to temporarily turn paid parking on part of Queen Street East into a commercial loading zone while the laneway behind businesses is rebuilt. The $3.25-per-hour spaces would return to their old rules after construction.

title: Mirvish Village - Traffic Amendments (Non-Delegated)
brief: Up for a decision before City Council: ban northbound left turns and southbound right turns at all times at Bathurst Street and the private driveway at 758 Bathurst Street, as part of the Mirvish Village traffic plan.

title: Call to Order
brief: City Council opens its meeting with O Canada and a moment of silence.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from City Officials
brief: City Council formally introduces the committee reports it will consider at this meeting.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: Council members declare any conflicts of interest under provincial law.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Petitions
brief: Council members may file petitions.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: Various presentations and announcements are made at the council meeting.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: City Council reviews the Order Paper listing its business.
stake: A citywide decision. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 21 in favour, none against.

title: Community Sports Equipment Sponsorship
brief: This is an information item: the committee receives a report on Jumpstart's proposal for sports equipment lending stations in parks, with at least one per community council area by summer 2026.
stake: About sponsorship. Decided by a recorded vote, 16 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Approach to Public Electric Vehicle (EV Charging) Three-Year Plan
topics: electric distribution utilities, electric scooters, electricity, parking
brief: The committee considers a 3-year EV charging plan through a city-Parking Authority-partner deal, with the partner investing an estimated $35.8 million. $1.5 billion is also cited.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $35.8 million.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: City Council confirms the minutes from its March 25 and 26, 2026 meeting.

title: Refreshing Food and Beverage Offerings in Park and Recreation Spaces
topics: food and beverage industry, parks, recreation centres
brief: Before Council for a decision: approve a park mobile vending program and let staff sign licence agreements for food stands in parks, as near-term steps toward a full food-and-drink strategy in 2027.

title: Repairs and Rehabilitation on Wilson Avenue Due to Contract BFPP (21 ECS-LU-04FP)
topics: business improvement areas, public realm, restoration
business improvement associations, public spaces, rehabilitation (property)
brief: Councillor Pasternak (Ward 6) asks Council to order immediate repairs to Wilson Avenue infrastructure damaged during water construction work.

title: Watermain Cleaning and Relining on Various Streets in the Sheppard Avenue / Chesswood Drive Area
brief: Councillor Pasternak (Ward 6) flags worries that watermain work on Sheppard Avenue and Chesswood Drive could disrupt businesses and Rogers Stadium concert traffic (52,200 seats, 17 May concerts).

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Toronto Zoo Board
brief: Recommending two candidates to City Council for the Toronto Zoo Board for a term ending March 28, 2030. It goes to the Civic Appointments Committee for a decision. Candidate details stay private.

title: Appointment of a Public Member to the Exhibition Place Board
brief: Recommending one candidate to City Council for the Exhibition Place Board for a term ending March 28, 2030. It goes to the Civic Appointments Committee for a decision. Candidate details stay private.

title: Prioritizing Expansion of Roseneath Park - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo asks council to prioritize expanding Roseneath Park near Oakwood and St. Clair West, a 2,340-square-metre park in one of the city's lowest parkland areas, where the city has already bought 252 Winona Drive.

title: Improving Pedestrian Safety at Ossington Avenue and Dupont Street - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo asks council to advance pedestrian safety fixes at Ossington Avenue and Dupont Street, where residents say speeding drivers nearly hit pedestrians, building on quick-build measures from October 2025.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.NY28.10 - 2925 Keele Street (Stanley Greene Block G) Subdivision - Assumption of Services, Correction to Reference Registered Plan 66M-2554 - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Jon Burnside
brief: This is procedural: council is asked to re-open a 2025 decision to fix a typo, changing Registered Plan 66M-2520 to 66M-2554, so the 2925 Keele Street subdivision's services can be formally assumed.

title: Legal Options to Defend City of Toronto's Interests at Billy Bishop Airport Lands and Other City-Owned Waterfront Lands
brief: City Council asked the City Solicitor for legal options to protect the City's interests in the Billy Bishop Airport lands and other City waterfront lands. The advice stays private.
stake: About airports. Decided by a recorded vote, 24 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: 1666 St. Clair Avenue West - Liquor Licence Application - Sporting Clube Portugues de Toronto - Licence 3605953 - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo asks council to tell the province's liquor regulator that the Sporting Clube Portugues de Toronto at 1666 St. Clair Ave West should not get a liquor licence unless conditions address residents' noise, litter and safety concerns.

title: Clarifying the Distinction Between Duplexes and Secondary Suites - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
brief: Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin asks council to clarify the line between duplexes and secondary suites, saying the current duplex definition lets applicants build effectively larger houses through a minimal basement unit.

title: Proclaiming November 19 as Early Age Onset Cancer Awareness Day - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
brief: Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin asks council to proclaim November 19 as Early Age Onset Cancer Awareness Day and run a public education campaign, citing rising cancer rates in Canadians born after 1980.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Sign Variance Committee
brief: Appointing Stephen Job and Farzana Jiwani to the Sign Variance Committee to April 24, 2030, and name Derek Lett as Chair to December 16, 2027. It goes to City Council for approval.

title: Appointment of Public Members to the Administrative Penalty Tribunal
brief: Appointing twelve members and Chair Paul Sommerville to the Administrative Penalty Tribunal to April 25, 2030. It goes to City Council for approval. The tribunal settles disputes over certain City fines.

title: Proclaiming April as Nepali Heritage Month - by Councillor Neethan Shan, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
brief: Councillor Neethan Shan asks council to proclaim April as Nepali Heritage Month in Toronto, and to ask the province and federal government to do the same.

title: Cricket Day - by Councillor Neethan Shan, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: Councillor Neethan Shan asks council to proclaim September 24, 2026 as Cricket Day and have staff engage cricket groups on events and better facilities.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds to the Wigmore Park Improvements Project - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
brief: Councillor Jon Burnside asks council to release $367,905.77 in parkland funds from the 1648 Victoria Park Avenue development for improvements at Wigmore Park.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $367,905.77.

title: Metrolinx Accountability on Joe Shuster Way Fence Graffiti and Public Art  - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik asks council to press Metrolinx for ongoing graffiti removal on its fence on Joe Shuster Way and a resident-designed community art plan as a long-term fix.

title: "Have Your Say" Amplified: Enhancing Public Consultations and Surveys - Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: Councillor Chris Moise asks council to require all city public consultations to be listed on Have Your Say, with central oversight, by the first quarter of 2027, so residents learn about them in time to take part.

title: Renewing Official Recognition of Toronto as a Certified Bird Friendly City - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik asks council to renew Toronto's Bird Friendly City certification through Nature Canada, which needs a council resolution.

title: Strengthening Racial Equity in City Programs and Services - by Councillor Neethan Shan, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: Councillor Neethan Shan asks council to strengthen racial equity in city programs, with a yearly public report on best practices and a possible racial justice advisory body reflecting Toronto's diversity.
stake: About equity. Decided by a recorded vote, 17 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: Responding to Bill 98, Building Homes and Improving Transportation Infrastructure Act, 2026 - by Councillor Jamaal Myers, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo

stake: About public transit. Council put off deciding this item.
