title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds to the Dieppe Park Baseball Lighting Improvements Project - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher asks council to release $170,000 for lighting upgrades at Dieppe Park's baseball diamond. The source also lists amounts of $20,000, $22,000, $18,000, $16,000, $25,000, $14,000 and $15,000.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $170,000.

title: Towards a Vision for a Design Standard for Future Toronto Subway Stations - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng asks council to develop a design vision for future subway stations as well-lit civic hubs with amenities and community space, pointing to examples like Taipei.
stake: About public transit. Decided by a recorded vote, 17 in favour and 4 against — every member's position is public.

title: Reinstating Paddle the Don for 2027 - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher asks council to request the return of Paddle the Don in 2027 and have city staff discuss supporting the event with the conservation authority.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Acquisition of Community Space in the Church Wellesley Village - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: Councillor Chris Moise asks council to authorize Section 37 funds to buy community space in the Church-Wellesley Village, where development pressure has shrunk room for 2SLGBTQ+ organizations. No dollar figure is in the source.
stake: Ward 13 is named in the record.

title: It’s Time to Reinstate Cummer Station for the North York Centre - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng asks council to push for reinstating Cummer Station on the Yonge North Subway Extension, which would otherwise leave a 2-kilometre gap between Finch and Steeles.
stake: About public transit. Decided by a recorded vote, 16 in favour and 7 against — every member's position is public.

title: Update on the Bathurst Quay Neighbourhood Transportation Study - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: This is procedural: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik asks council to fold a Bathurst Quay transportation update into a spring 2026 report on the Billy Bishop Airport flightpath expansion.

title: Urgent Action to Address Safety and Public Realm Conditions at 464-470 Queen Street West - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik asks council to have staff work with the developer on immediate fencing safety fixes at the future park site at 464-470 Queen Street West, where blown-over fencing blocks the sidewalk ahead of summer FIFA activity.

title: Community Engagement Process to Assess Local Community Support for Echoes and Nighttime Closure of Barbara Hall Park - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: Councillor Chris Moise asks council to run community engagement on options for Barbara Hall Park, including nighttime closure, amid persistent safety concerns around the AIDS Memorial and Trans Memorial.
stake: About parks. Decided by a recorded vote, 6 in favour and 17 against — every member's position is public.

title: Support for Minister’s Zoning Order (MZO) to Maintain Lands in the City of Toronto as Employment Lands to Protect the Ontario Food Terminal - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: Councillor Amber Morley asks council to support the province's proposed zoning order keeping 125 The Queensway as employment lands to protect the Ontario Food Terminal, which supports 2,500 direct and about 168,000 indirect jobs.

title: Accepting a Donation from the Friends of University Avenue for the Lighting Installation at University Median Park, Between Elm Street and College Street on University Avenue - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe asks council to accept a $755,000.00 in-kind donation of the University Avenue median lighting installation plus $32,500.00 cash from the Friends of University Avenue: $30,000.00 for maintenance and $2,500.00 for fall flowers, for a combined $787,500.00.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $755,000.00.

title: Direction to Finalize Section 37 Agreement for 765 Steeles Avenue West - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng asks council to give the city more flexibility over the design and use of community space secured through Section 37 at 765 Steeles Avenue West.

title: Cabbagetown Cycling Connects - Ontario Street Parking By-law Amendments - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: Councillor Chris Moise asks council to approve parking by-law changes for the Ontario Street cycling connection in Cabbagetown, adding contra-flow bike lanes and a loading zone while keeping curbside parking.

title: Ward-Based Maintenance Teams Pilot - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
brief: Councillor Anthony Perruzza asks council to pilot ward-based maintenance teams handling potholes, litter, grass, tree trimming and sidewalk repairs, with a report back at the next council meeting.

title: Enforcing the Westray Amendments to Keep Workers Safe - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow asks council to push the province and the police board to train and resource enforcement of the Westray criminal-negligence law protecting workers, timed to the April 28 Day of Mourning.

title: Applegrove Community Complex: Update on Relocation Options
brief: This is for information only: council receives an update on relocation options for the Applegrove Community Complex. One attachment stays private because it involves a possible property purchase.

title: 2461 to 2475 Dundas Street West - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on a Tribunal hearing about a 29-storey building with 288 homes at 2461 to 2475 Dundas Street West, refused by Council in 2024. Details stay private as legal advice.

title: 110 Sheppard Avenue East - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on a Tribunal hearing about two proposed towers (49 and 53 storeys) with 1,313 homes at 110 Sheppard Avenue East. Details stay private as legal advice.

title: 59 to 81 Lawton Boulevard - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on a June 8, 2026 Tribunal hearing about two proposed towers (38 and 43 storeys) at 59 to 81 Lawton Boulevard. Details stay private as legal advice.

title: 34 to 70 Montgomery Avenue - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Consent to Review Tribunal Decision
brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for permission to have a land-dispute board review its 2024 decision about 34 to 70 Montgomery Avenue. Details stay private as legal advice.

brief: Approving paying back $20,807.61 in legal costs to Councillor Chris Moise, spent answering a recent Integrity Commissioner investigation. It goes to City Council for approval.
stake: About refund. Decided by a recorded vote, 11 in favour and 4 against — every member's position is public.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026: Non-Competitive Procurement with the FIFA Fan Festival Toronto vendor
brief: Council has the final say on whether to authorize a no-bid $9.0 million increase with the existing FIFA Fan Festival Toronto vendor for extra services, at no net cost to the City, on top of the vendor's $16.0 million contract. The report's figures also include $380.0 million, $25.0 million, $500,000, and $7.1 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $16.0 million. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 22 in favour, none against.

title: Implementation of O.Reg 1/26 under the Liquor Licence and Control Act, 2019 in the City of Toronto
brief: Councillor Bravo asks council to have the City Clerk and Economic Development and Culture report to the April 22, 2026 meeting on the by-law changes needed to put in place the province's expanded bring-your-own liquor permits for cultural and community events.

title: Fighting for the Scarborough East Rapid Transit Line
brief: Mayor Chow asks council to make the Scarborough East Rapid Transit Line its top unfunded transit priority, ask the province and federal government to each pay one-third of the cost, and add $10 million to the 2026 transit expansion budget. The report's figures also include $2 billion, $18 million, $4.3 million, $45 million, and $377.9 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $2 billion. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 25 in favour, none against.

brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on a Tribunal hearing about the City taking the land at 1430 Gerrard Street East for permanent affordable rental homes. Details stay private as legal advice.

title: Addressing Inaccurate Supporting Documentation Submitted to the Committee of Adjustment - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin asks council to have staff report back in early 2027 on how the accuracy of supporting documents filed with Committee of Adjustment applications is verified.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds to the Ferrand Park Improvements Project - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Brad Bradford
brief: Councillor Jon Burnside asks council to release $439,600 in parkland funds from the 1185 Eglinton Avenue East development for improvements at Ferrand Park.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $439,600.

title: Financial Assistance for Covenant House’s Redevelopment Project at 20 Gerrard Street East and 21 McGill Street - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: Councillor Chris Moise asks council to provide financial assistance for Covenant House Toronto's redevelopment at 20 Gerrard St E and 21 McGill St into about 118 supportive and transitional youth homes. No dollar figure is in the source.

title: Authorization to Release Section 42 Funds for Advancing Safety Improvements Through an Upgraded Playground Structure at Canoe Landing - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik asks council to release $450,000.00 in parkland funds for a replacement playground at Canoe Landing, after the old structure was removed as unsafe following two 2025 injuries.

title: State of Good Repair at the Jarvis and Sherbourne Underpasses Within the Union Station Rail Corridor - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik asks council to authorize a deal for up to $500,000 from Metrolinx toward upkeep of the Lower Jarvis and Lower Sherbourne rail underpasses. The source lists $280,000 and $220,000 amounts alongside the total.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $500,000.

title: Community Mailboxes: Protecting our Public Space - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow asks council to set a second-quarter 2026 deadline on its community mailbox requests to Canada Post and push to recoup city costs, insisting mailboxes be safe, accessible and well-maintained.

title: 109 Knox Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: This is procedural: council is asked to let the City Solicitor appear before the Toronto Local Appeal Body over the refused third and fourth-storey additions at 109 Knox Avenue.

title: Requesting an Equitable Approach to the Canada Post Community Mailbox Conversions in Ward 1 - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
brief: Councillor Vincent Crisanti asks council to seek a pause and an equitable plan for Canada Post's mailbox conversions in Etobicoke North, the only Toronto area converting in late 2026 and early 2027, to protect seniors and people with accessibility needs.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Midtown Yonge Business Improvement Area for Implementation Two Interactive Public Murals at 2075 Yonge Street and 1980 Yonge Street - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow asks council to give the Midtown Yonge BIA $48,000.00 ($48,000) in developer funds for two interactive murals at 2075 and 1980 Yonge Street, painted live at the June 20, 2026 Arraia on Yonge Festival.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $48,000.00.

title: Starting Construction of the Waterfront East Rapid Transit Line in 2026 - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow asks council to authorize funding and governance to start building the Waterfront East Rapid Transit Line in 2026, with $2 billion in provincial and federal money matching the city's $1 billion. The source also lists $70 million.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $2 billion.

brief: Councillor James Pasternak asks council to review notification rules for major film-production explosions near homes, after an April 16, 2026 Downsview blast frightened residents who feared an industrial accident.

title: Amending Item 2025.TE19.8 - 1 to 19 Thelma Avenue - Rental Housing Demolition Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle

brief: This is procedural: council is asked to re-open a November 2025 decision and narrow a full-time College Street no-stopping zone between Dufferin and Gladstone to rush hours only, after businesses reported delivery and access problems. The motion also lists $3.25.

title: Improving the City’s Laneway Conveyance Process - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: Councillor Josh Matlow asks council to fix the city's laneway conveyance process, where unclear roles and timelines across divisions are delaying developments including 2010 to 2050 Yonge and 15 Lola Road.

brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher asks council to recognize Claude Cormier's five waterfront parks with a Love Parade celebration and a May 2026 bike tour.

title: Opposing the Provincial Land Grab at Bathurst Quay and the Island - by Mayor Olivia Chow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: Mayor Olivia Chow asks council to oppose provincial legislation transferring city land at Toronto Island and Bathurst and Queen's Quay to the province, citing concerns about Little Norway Park and council's March vote against unilateral expropriation.
stake: About land. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 25 in favour, none against.

brief: City buying staff will present a proposed policy for First Nations, Inuit and Métis businesses, including how it would make it easier for them to bid on City work.

brief: City environment staff will present plans for an Indigenous Table to guide the division's work, centred on Indigenous governance and ways of working, and ask the committee for feedback.
stake: About First Nations. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

topics: First Nations, aboriginal services, advisory committees, personal identification

topics: Toronto Transit Commission, labour relations, unions

topics: Exhibition Place, information and communication technology, security
brief: A decision on approving a new IT information security policy, developed in response to the Auditor General's cybersecurity audit, with a yearly review cycle sits with the Exhibition Place board.

brief: This is for information only: the board receives the year-end report on the 2025 building works program, a $113,214,108 budget covering $24,276,213 in state-of-good-repair projects, a $2,250,013 carry forward, and $86,687,882 for BMO Field improvements supporting the FIFA World Cup. No policy change is proposed.

brief: Before the Exhibition Place board for a decision: approve a $1,366,078.15 contract (including a $20,000.00 cash allowance) with Century Group Inc. to upgrade salons 103, 105, 109 and 110 at the Enercare Centre. It was the only compliant bid.

brief: Approving a $3,818,063.00 contract with Triumph Roofing and Sheet Metal Inc. to replace the leaking roofs of Horse Palace East and the vehicle maintenance garage, which are worn out is on the Exhibition Place board's agenda. brief: This is for information only: the board receives a report on the collaboration with Heritage Toronto celebrating the history of women's sport at Exhibition Place. No policy change is proposed.

brief: Before the board for a decision: endorse a vision plan for the Exhibition Place grounds, have the CEO work with the City on planning and financing options with a report by 2027, and develop a community engagement plan by late 2026.

topics: Exhibition Place, public transit, regional transportation agencies
brief: This is for information only: the board receives a Metrolinx update on the Ontario Line, a 15.6 km subway with 15 stations running from Exhibition Place to Eglinton Avenue East and Don Mills Road. No decision is proposed.

title: Litigation Update
brief: This is a routine item. The TTC Board will get a private update on large lawsuits with at least $500,000.00 at stake and keep the details confidential.

brief: The TTC Board will get an update on the fare collection deal with Metrolinx, which expires November 28, 2027, after Metrolinx opted out of renewing it.

brief: The TTC Board will vote on updates to the CEO's spending authority, keeping single-source contracts at $500,000 and reporting awards over $5 million, with a $2.5 million figure also cited.

topics: Toronto Transit Commission, archives (records), conservation (archival), records

brief: The TTC Board will consider the TTC's response to Bill 98, the provincial Building Homes and Improving Transportation Infrastructure Act, 2026.

topics: Toronto Transit Commission, accessibility, light rail transit, public service announcements
brief: The TTC Board will decide the TTC's position on a dispute over audible stop announcements on Line 5 and Line 6, where Metrolinx owns the vehicles.

brief: This is a routine item. The TTC Board will review the CEO's performance and objectives and keep the details confidential.

topics: Toronto Transit Commission, advisory committees, audits, committee meetings

brief: This is a routine item. The TTC Board will hear a presentation on FIFA World Cup 2026 preparations.
stake: About Toronto Transit Commission. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Motion without Notice - Addressing Fluid Leaks and Mechanical Service Disruptions to Ensure Better Service Reliability on the TTC - by Commissioner Josh Matlow, seconded by Chair Jamaal Myers
brief: The TTC Board will consider a motion on April's fluid leaks and service disruptions on Line 2, which references $37 billion in capital needs.

brief: The Service Excellence Committee asks the Executive Committee to have the City Manager report by early 2027 on requiring City divisions to develop fix-up plans when service performance standards are missed or gaps persist.

title: Amendment to Purchase Order 6043796 with WSP Canada Inc., and Purchase Order 6052068 with Maple Reinders Constructors Limited for Rehabilitation and Upgrades of Seven Group Six Sewage Pumping Stations at Various Locations
brief: The city wants to add $1,599,436 ($1,627,586 net of HST recoveries) to WSP's pumping station contract. It would rise from $2,923,091 ($2,974,537 net of HST recoveries) to $4,522,527 ($4,602,123 net of HST recoveries). The city also wants to add $2,000,000 ($2,035,200) to Maple Reinders' contract, raising it from $27,646,800 ($28,133,384 net of HST recoveries) to $29,646,800 ($30,168,584 net of HST recoveries). $1,300,000 is also cited.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1,599,436.

title: Litigation Arising from the Construction of the St. Lawrence Market North
brief: The builders of St. Lawrence Market North are suing the city for $81,448,497.40 plus HST over construction delays; the city has defended and counterclaimed ($8,307,084.19 cited). The committee handles the litigation item.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $81,448,497.40.

title: Non-Competitive Contract with Grascan Construction Ltd., for Emergency Soffit Shoring Repairs to the F.G. Gardiner Expressway
brief: The city reports an emergency no-bid contract with Grascan Construction worth $4,275,568 ($4,350,818 net of HST recoveries) to shore up crumbling concrete under the Gardiner Expressway.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $4,275,568.

title: Renewal of Various Boat Club Leases
topics: boat facilities, boating, boating clubs, recreational watercraft
brief: Renewing leases for 24 non-profit volunteer-run boat clubs on the waterfront for up to 20 years each. It goes to City Council for approval. The leases would bring the city about $849,590 in rent in 2026, rising with inflation each year.
stake: About boat facilities. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 5 against — every member's position is public.

title: A Portion of 550 Bayview Avenue (Evergreen Brick Works) Evergreen Lease Amendment and Extension Agreement
brief: Approving a 20-year lease extension with Evergreen for Evergreen Brick Works at 550 Bayview Avenue, plus a licence for underground geothermal works. It goes to City Council for approval.

title: A Programmatic Approach to Delivering State of Good Repair, Accessibility, and Net Zero Programs at City Hall and Metro Hall
topics: accessibility, city-owned properties, maintenance, programs, properties (real estate)
brief: Council is asked to let a senior city official approve contract changes over $500,000 for the City Hall and Metro Hall repair, accessibility, and net-zero program, within its $300 million budget. Staff would report back twice a year.

title: Pothole Blitz and Local Road Repair Strategy
brief: Mayor Chow asks council to have Transportation Services run an ongoing pothole blitz based on road conditions and 311 data, building on the Fixing Roads Faster program, which has $11 million in new 2026 funding.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $11 million. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 24 in favour, none against.

title: Port Lands Flood Protection Project: Update and Next Steps
brief: Council decides whether to authorize a lease or licence with the Toronto Port Lands Company for lands needed for early works on Ookwemin Minising Phase 1, after the Port Lands Flood Protection project reached substantial completion in September 2025.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Heliconian Club - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe asks council to release $30,000 in developer funds to repair the carved wood details of the Heliconian Hall at 35 Hazelton Avenue, the 1876 home of the women's arts club and a National Historic Site.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Benches and Wayfinding at Toronto Transit Commission Stations - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe asks council to give the TTC $100,000 in developer funds for 31 three-seat benches at eight Line 2 stations from Castle Frank to Christie, plus better wayfinding at Yonge-Bloor, St. George and Spadina.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $100,000.

title: Non-Competitive Extension with Carla Construction & Maintenance Ltd., for Trackless Train Service in High Park for Parks and Recreation
topics: Toronto Transit Commission, construction, contracts, parks, trains
brief: Extending the High Park trackless train deal with Carla Construction & Maintenance Ltd for the 2026 season without bidding, after a shuttle tender fell through. It goes to City Council for approval.

title: Update on Weston Foundation Donation for Queen's Park North Revitalization
brief: It's Council's call whether to authorize accepting a donation of up to $50 million from the Weston Foundation to fund the final design and delivery of the Queen's Park North revitalization. The report's figures also include $500,000.

title: Toronto Wins Bloomberg Philanthropies 2025 - 2026 Mayors Challenge
brief: Toronto won the Bloomberg Philanthropies 2025-2026 Mayors Challenge prize of $1.4 million for its school food program vision, one of 24 winners from 630 cities. Council approved receiving the award — USD $1.2 million (about CAD $1,643,720) — for a universal school food program. The letter also notes a $7 million budget boost for school food programs and almost $900 in savings for families with two kids.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1.4 million. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 23 in favour, none against.

title: Metrolinx Subway Program Update - 2026
topics: executive committees, regional transportation agencies, subways
brief: Up for a decision before Council: authorize the City Manager to amend the Subway Program Real Estate Protocol with Metrolinx and to give approval power for small temporary construction licences, for the four subway expansion projects.

title: Emergency Non-Competitive Contract with Webber Infrastructure Management Canada Limited for Snow Removal Services
topics: agreements, contracts, snow emergencies, snow management, snow removal
snow plans, snow emergency, snow melting
brief: The city reports an emergency no-bid snow removal contract with Webber Infrastructure worth $942,425 ($959,012 net of HST recoveries) after January 2026 storms dropped about 90 centimetres of snow.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $942,425.

title: Call to Order
brief: City Council opens its meeting with O Canada and a moment of silence.

title: Confirmation of Minutes
brief: City Council confirms the minutes from its December 2025 and February 2026 meetings.

title: Short Term Parking at the Price Street Green P Lot - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe asks council to have the Toronto Parking Authority turn at least 20 of the 71 Price Street Green P spots into three-hour short-term parking for local restaurant and business customers, as construction workers' cars fill the lot all day.

title: Council Member Appointments to the Canadian National Exhibition Association Municipal Section and Board of Directors
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council can appoint five of its members to the Canadian National Exhibition Association board, starting spring 2026.

title: Council Member Appointment to Fill a Vacancy on the Aboriginal Affairs Advisory Committee
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council can appoint one of its members to fill a vacancy on the Aboriginal Affairs Advisory Committee.

title: Council Member Appointments to Fill Vacancies on the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority Board of Directors
brief: This is a procedural item: City Council can appoint three of its members to the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority board.

title: Introduction of Committee Reports and New Business from City Officials
brief: City Council formally introduces the committee reports it will consider at this meeting.

title: Declarations of Interest
brief: Council members declare any conflicts of interest under provincial law.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Petitions
brief: Council members may file petitions.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Presentations, Introductions and Announcements
brief: Various presentations and announcements are made at the council meeting.
stake: A citywide decision. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: Review of the Order Paper
brief: City Council reviews the Order Paper listing its business.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Toronto Public Library - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe asks council to put $110,605.48 of Section 37 funds, originally $103,251.33 set aside in 2005, toward public art at the Toronto Reference Library's coming Centre for Democracy.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $103,251.33.

title: Winter Surge Capacity Snow Shovellers
brief: Mayor Chow asks council to have staff develop a paid surge sidewalk-shovelling program, modelled on New York City's approach, to start no later than the 2026-2027 winter season, to help clear sidewalks after extreme storms.
stake: About snow ploughing. Decided by a recorded vote, 21 in favour and 5 against — every member's position is public.

title: Supporting the Role of Trustees in Maintaining an Accountable and Transparent Education System - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Amber Morley
brief: Councillors Chernos Lin and Morley ask Council to support the role of elected school trustees after Ontario replaced trustees with appointed supervisors in summer 2025.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Toronto Community Housing Corporation for Affordable Housing Upgrades - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe asks council to release $2,366,000 ($2,366,000.00) in developer funds for upgrades at seven Toronto Community Housing buildings in Ward 11: $225,000 at 250 Davenport Rd, $846,000 at 177 Pendrith St, $275,000 at 40 Asquith Ave, $400,000 at 341 Bloor St, $310,000 at 25 Elm St, $220,000 at 72 Clinton St and $90,000 at 34 Oxford St, covering security cameras, landscaping, lighting and solar panels. The report also lists $84,634, $260,722, $110,000, $32,997, $168,420, $474,164, $817,366 and $417,697 as additional listed figures.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $225,000.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to the Huron Street Garden - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Lily Cheng
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe asks council to create a $57,263 project for the Huron Street Garden, now Lillian H. Smith Park, covering a garden shed, picnic table, three benches, a sign and three raised planters, from $50,000 in Section 37 funds set aside in 2015.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $50,000.

title: Urgent Action on Violent Residential Break-Ins and Organized Crime Auto Thefts - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
topics: break-in, crime, police officers, police services boards
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe asks council to have the police chief report back on armed home invasions tied to organized car theft, and on what police are doing to stop them.

title: Cracking Down on Bad Landlords
brief: Mayor Chow asks council to have the City Manager create a public database tracking enforcement at rental properties with multiple complaints by July 2026, and to set up ongoing coordination on problem buildings.
stake: About housing. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 26 in favour, none against.

title: 180 Queens Drive - Proposed Designation By-law Under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act - Consideration of Objection
brief: Confirming its plan to protect 180 Queens Drive under the Heritage Act, despite the owner's objection, and to let the City Solicitor introduce the law. It goes to City Council for approval.

title: 895 Lawrence Avenue East - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on a Tribunal hearing about a two-tower, 438-home project at 895 Lawrence Ave East. The advice stays private as legal advice.
stake: About zoning bylaws. Decided by a recorded vote, 23 in favour and 1 against — every member's position is public.

title: 435 Ellerslie Avenue - Appeal of Property Standards Order - Folder Number 26 107449 PRS 00 IV
brief: This is a procedural item: the Property Standards Committee will hear an appeal of a property standards order for 435 Ellerslie Avenue, issued January 26, 2026.

title: Improving Design Quality and Neighbourhood Fit of As-of-Right Multiplex Housing - by Councillor James Pasternak, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
brief: Councillor James Pasternak asks council to have city planners review how new as-of-right multiplexes look and fit into low-rise neighbourhoods, and to consider ways to improve their design.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for 2025 Participatory Budgeting Projects for St. Lawrence Neighbourhoods - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: Councillor Chris Moise asks council to release $750,000 in developer funds for seven resident-voted heritage projects in the St. Lawrence area: plaques, heritage street signs and banners, and shoreline commemoration projects. The official text lists project amounts of $500,000.00, $80,000.00, $585,000, $10,000, $5,000.00, $4,000.00 and $2,400.00.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $750,000.

title: Designation of the Kensington Market Heritage Conservation District Under Part V of the Ontario Heritage Act - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing
brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on appeals of the Kensington Market heritage district designation, ahead of a June 1, 2026 hearing. The advice stays private as legal advice.

title: 320 McCowan Road - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on a Tribunal settlement about the zoning change for 320 McCowan Road. The advice stays private as legal advice.

title: 233 Carlton Street
brief: Councillor Moise (Ward 13) filed an inquiry asking for a public update on delays and costs for the leased 233 Carlton Street drop-in site, which has not opened since 2020.
stake: About community centres. Received for information — Council took no action on it.

title: 40 to 62 Spadina Avenue and 378 Wellington Street West - Official Plan Amendment and Zoning By-law Amendment - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on a Tribunal hearing about a 30-storey building at 40-62 Spadina Ave and 378 Wellington St West. The advice stays private.

title: Ookwemin Minising - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Direction
brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on a Tribunal hearing about the planning rules for Ookwemin Minising, the Port Lands island. The advice stays private as legal advice.

title: 444 to 468 Eglinton Avenue West - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on a Tribunal matter about 444-468 Eglinton Ave West, where the Tribunal dismissed the appeal of a revised 31-storey, 322-home proposal in July 2025 and told the parties to work toward a resolution. The advice stays private as legal advice.
stake: About appeals. Decided by a recorded vote, 24 in favour and 2 against — every member's position is public.

title: Legal Advice Regarding City of Vaughan v. 7553 Islington Holding Inc.
brief: The City Solicitor asks Council to approve private instructions about legal advice on a Tribunal decision for 155 St. Dennis Drive and a related matter in Vaughan.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for 2025 Participatory Budgeting Projects for Bay Cloverhill, Bloor East, Church Wellesley and Upper Jarvis Neighbourhoods - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: Councillor Chris Moise asks council to release $750,000 in developer funds for two resident-voted park projects: the Wellesley-Magill Park revitalization ($250,000.00) and a small-dogs off-leash area at James Canning Park ($500,000.00).
stake: The official summary names a figure of $750,000.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for 2025 Participatory Budgeting Projects for Canary District, Corktown, and Distillery District Neighbourhoods - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: Councillor Chris Moise asks council to release $750,000 in developer funds for three resident-voted projects in Canary District, Corktown and the Distillery: reimagining Lawren Harris Square ($680,000.00), plus an all-weather ping pong table and more seating at Corktown Commons ($10,000.00).
stake: The official summary names a figure of $750,000.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for Schoolyard Improvements at Brock Public School - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo asks council to release $30,000 in developer funds for schoolyard improvements at Brock Public School in Davenport.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 to Heritage Toronto for Streetscape Improvements - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Jamaal Myers
brief: Councillor Amber Morley asks council to give Heritage Toronto $10,000 for a plaque at Islington station marking where the prehistoric Toronto Subway Deer antlers were found in 1976.
stake: Ward 3 is named in the record.

title: Authorization to Release of Section 37 Funds for the Preservation of the Zhong Hua Men Archway - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Frances Nunziata
brief: Councillor Paula Fletcher asks council to release $28,638.23 in developer funds to preserve the Zhong Hua Men Archway, the gateway to East Chinatown at Broadview and Gerrard.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $28,638.23.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.TE22.3 - 72 Perth Avenue - Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Decision Report - Approval - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Gord Perks
brief: This is procedural: council is asked to re-open its 72 Perth Avenue approval to fix a parkland dedication that measures 131 square metres instead of the required 134, with a possible Building Code restriction on part of the land.

title: Amending Item 2021.TE25.3 - 111 to 125 River Street - Zoning Amendment and Rental Housing Demolition Applications - Final Report - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Shelley Carroll
brief: Councillor Chris Moise asks council to re-open a 2021 decision so the owner of 111 to 125 River Street can demolish five vacant rental units now for health and safety reasons, with an interim community use explored for the lot.

title: 506 to 516 Church Street - Official Plan and Zoning By-law Amendment Application - Ontario Land Tribunal Hearing - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on a Tribunal hearing about the 48-storey building at 506-516 Church St, refused in February 2025. The advice stays private. The settlement offer includes a $2,000,000 payment from the developer for community facilities and recreation space.

title: Interest Arbitration Results with Toronto Professional Firefighters' Association, Local 3888
brief: Approving budget changes from interest arbitration with the Toronto firefighters' union, whose contract ended in 2023. It goes to City Council for approval. Details stay private because it is about labour talks.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds to Commemorate Arena Gardens - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Stephen Holyday
brief: Councillor Chris Moise asks council to give Heritage Toronto $10,000 for a plaque at 78 Mutual Street honouring Arena Gardens, the original home of Toronto's NHL team.

title: Appointment of Interim Deputy City Managers, Infrastructure Services and Corporate Services
brief: Appointing two temporary Deputy City Managers, one for Infrastructure Services and one for Corporate Services, starting April 3, 2026. It goes to City Council for approval. The names are in private documents.

title: Grocery Store Pilot Project - by Councillor Anthony Perruzza, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: Councillor Anthony Perruzza asks council to pilot four city-run grocery stores, one per Community Council district, prioritizing areas with poor access to affordable groceries, to fight food insecurity.
stake: A citywide decision. Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 4 against — every member's position is public.

title: Re-opening and Amending Item 2025.TE21.33 - Accessible Parking Space - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
brief: This is procedural: council is asked to re-open an April 2025 decision and restore an accessible parking space on Dundas Street West near Coolmine Road, after the original applicant withdrew the concern that got it removed.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds for the Revitalization of Moss Park Arena - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: Councillor Chris Moise asks council to release $300,000 ($300,000.00) in developer funds for extras in the Moss Park Arena revitalization: a new refrigeration plant, two electric Zambonis, and lighting, washroom and changeroom upgrades.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $300,000.

title: Update of Definition and Reporting of the Delegated Authority on Certain Real Estate Matters - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by James Pasternak
brief: Councillor Chris Moise asks council to update the rules and reporting for delegated real-estate decisions, after cost details emerged on the $6 million, 15-year lease at 233 Carlton Street: a $3.7 million initial renovation estimate, over $2 million in rent paid, an $8.7 million contractor award, and $13.5 million in forecasted costs, above the $10 million threshold.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $6 million.

title: Amending the Composition of the Board of Health Due To Provincial Supervision of School Boards - by Councillor Chris Moise, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: This is procedural: council is asked to remove the vacant school-board seat from the Board of Health and add a citizen member instead, because the province put school boards under supervision in June 2025 and the board is struggling to reach quorum.
stake: About boards of health. The item was withdrawn before a final decision.

title: 1312 St. Clair Avenue West - Liquor Licence Application - Alpine Espresso Bar Number 3388560 - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo asks council to tell the province's liquor regulator that Alpine Espresso Bar at 1312 St. Clair Ave West should not get a liquor licence unless conditions are attached, after residents raised noise, litter and safety concerns.

title: One Country, One Flag; Celebrating the Canadian Flag - by Councillor Jon Burnside, seconded by Councillor Michael Thompson
brief: Councillor Jon Burnside asks council to change its flag policy: no more foreign nations' flags or non-profit and charity flags on city poles, while keeping raisings for Indigenous and Treaty partners, the Intersex Pride and Black Liberation flags, sports teams and alliance cities.
stake: About flag raising. Decided by a recorded vote, 19 in favour and 7 against — every member's position is public.

title: Response to the Fire in Thorncliffe Park: Best Practices in Community Partnership - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin asks council to review lessons learned and best practices from the November 27, 2025 Thorncliffe Park fire, which displaced residents of nearly 400 units for more than a month.

title: Authority to Waive Permit Fees for Toronto District School Board and Toronto Catholic District School Board for Use of David Crombie Park - by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik asks council to waive permit fees for two schools temporarily using David Crombie Park's Block 3 during construction. The source lists fee amounts of $31,994.79, $4,299.78, $21,354.69 and $2,729.58.

title: Site-specific By-law to Enable a Property Tax Exemption for Thunder Woman Healing Lodge Society at 28 Algoma Street - by Councilor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: This is procedural: council is asked to pass a site-specific by-law so an approved property tax exemption takes effect for the Thunder Woman Healing Lodge Society's affordable housing at 28 Algoma Street, with tenants moving in March 30, 2026.

title: Evaluating Changes to Mute Swan Management in Etobicoke-Lakeshore - by Councillor Amber Morley, Seconded by Councillor Josh Matlow
brief: Councillor Amber Morley asks council to evaluate changes to the mute swan egg-oiling program run by the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority, citing research questioning the program and an 81 percent population drop since 2011, from 413 to 80 birds.
stake: About ecology. Decided by a recorded vote, 20 in favour and 4 against — every member's position is public.

title: Raising of the Lion and Sun Flag in Solidarity with Iranian-Canadians - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Nick Mantas
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng asks council to raise the historic Lion and Sun flag in solidarity with Iranian-Canadians, following resident requests and similar raisings in Aurora, Barrie, Richmond Hill and Vaughan.

title: Addressing Recycling in Public Spaces - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng asks council to have staff explore either restoring real recycling in public spaces or removing the 15,000 public Blue Bins, since the province's Blue Box takeover means their contents now go to landfill.
stake: About environment (sc). Decided by a recorded vote, 22 in favour and 4 against — every member's position is public.

title: 46 Spadina Avenue, 58 Spadina Avenue and 378 Wellington Street West - Alterations to and Demolition of Buildings at Heritage Properties Designated Under Part V of the Ontario Heritage Act - Request for Directions
brief: The City Solicitor asks Council for direction on a Tribunal matter about changes to heritage buildings at 46 and 58 Spadina and 378 Wellington. The advice stays private.

title: Addressing Limits of Sidewalk Construction on Taber Road - by Councillor Vincent Crisanti, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
brief: Councillor Vincent Crisanti asks council to shorten a planned 2026 sidewalk on the north side of Taber Road so it ends at the Rexdale Community Health Centre, addressing business concerns about lost parking while keeping the busiest pedestrian stretch.

title: Tax Credit Program for Vulnerable Community Institution Security Costs - by Councillor Mike Colle, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
brief: Councillor Mike Colle asks council to explore a tax credit to help vulnerable community institutions, like schools, synagogues and community centres, cover rising security costs. No dollar figure is attached.

title: 210 Cosburn Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Paula Fletcher, seconded by Councillor Alejandra Bravo
brief: This is procedural: council is asked to let the City Solicitor appeal a decision allowing four new basement units at 210 Cosburn Avenue, over missing amenity space and a parking drop from 26 to 16 spaces.

title: 99 Patricia Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor James Pasternak
brief: This is procedural: council is asked to let the City Solicitor appeal the approval of a fourplex and garden suite at 99 Patricia Avenue, after planning staff recommended refusing two height variances. The appeal deadline is March 25, 2026.

title: Introduction of General Bills and Confirming Bills
brief: This is routine business. City Council will introduce general bills and confirming bills, which formally enact Council's decisions as by-laws.

title: Report on Councillor Chris Moise’s Comments to a Constituent
brief: The Integrity Commissioner found Councillor Chris Moise broke the Code of Conduct by speaking harshly to a constituent, and asks City Council to accept the findings but give no penalty.
stake: About councillors. Its recorded vote was unanimous — 23 in favour, none against.

title: Authorization to Release Section 37 Funds from the Development at 2, 4 and 6 Teagarden Court for Improvements to the Schoolyard at St. Gabriel Catholic School - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng asks council to direct $50,000.00 in developer funds to St. Gabriel Catholic School's schoolyard in Willowdale, with a 20-year agreement keeping it open to the community outside school hours.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $50,000.00.

title: Authorization to Release Section 45 Funds to Parks and Recreation for McNicoll Park Basketball Court Improvements - by Councillor Shelley Carroll, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: Councillor Shelley Carroll asks council to approve up to $500,000.00 in developer funds for long-term renewal of the McNicoll Park basketball court, on top of $125,000.00 already set aside for near-term repairs. The source also lists a $250,000.00 figure.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $125,000.00.

title: Addressing Urgent Parking Capacity Gap at 175, 185 and 205 Cummer Avenue (Cummer Lodge, Willowdale Manor, and Seniors Supportive Housing) - by Councillor Lily Cheng, seconded by Councillor Vincent Crisanti
brief: Councillor Lily Cheng asks council to address the parking shortage at the seniors' campus of 175, 185 and 205 Cummer Avenue, home to Cummer Lodge, Willowdale Manor and a new supportive housing building, where doctors, caregivers and families struggle to find spots.
stake: About parking. Decided by a recorded vote, 17 in favour and 8 against — every member's position is public.

title: Waiving Permit Fees to Support the Bum Run - by Councillor Dianne Saxe, seconded by Councillor Chris Moise
brief: Councillor Dianne Saxe asks council to waive $5,209.14 in road-closure permit fees for the April 26, 2026 Bum Run, a charity run that has raised more than $1.8 million for colon cancer research and screening.
stake: The official summary names a figure of $1.8 million.

title: 35 Elder Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Amber Morley, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: This is procedural: council is asked to let the City Solicitor oppose the owner's appeal of a refused lot severance at 35 Elder Avenue before the Toronto Local Appeal Body, with a hearing already scheduled.

title: 2 to 20 Glazebrook Avenue and 391 Broadway Avenue - Request for City Solicitor to Attend at the Toronto Local Appeal Body - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Mike Colle
brief: This is procedural: council is asked to have the City Solicitor attend the Toronto Local Appeal Body over approved variances raising a North York building at 2-20 Glazebrook Avenue and 391 Broadway Avenue from 33 to 37 storeys and from 428 to 489 units. The source is truncated on the exact direction.

title: Maintaining Toronto’s Climate and Energy Priorities Through the Review Process for Artificial Intelligence Data Centre Proposals - by Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin, seconded by Councillor Dianne Saxe
brief: Councillor Rachel Chernos Lin asks council to make sure proposed artificial intelligence data centres are reviewed against Toronto's climate, energy, water and affordability goals, given their heavy power and water demands.

title: Options for Section 37 Agreement Contributions at Bloor and Dufferin - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Mayor Olivia Chow
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo asks council to have staff report back on taking a cash contribution instead of a pedestrian tunnel to Dufferin Station from the Bloor and Dufferin development, since tunnel costs have risen sharply. No dollar figure is set yet.

title: Closing Roads for Watermain Work Requires Proper Notice - by Councillor Alejandra Bravo, seconded by Councillor Paula Fletcher
brief: Councillor Alejandra Bravo asks council to require proper notice for watermain road closures, after Dupont Street was shut from February 24 to 27, 2026 with no warning to the councillor, businesses or the TTC.

title: Fighting for Ontario Place and Ontario’s Democracy - by Councillor Josh Matlow, seconded by Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik

The source tables cite hundreds of additional line-item figures not summarized here.
